INTRODUCTION
 
 
        I,      the Chairman of the Committee on Subordinate Legislation, having been authorized by the Committee to
present the Report on its behalf, do hereby present this Hundred and Fortieth Report of the Committee.
 
        1.2   The Committee considered and adopted the Report in its meeting held on February 11, 2002.
 
        1.3           The matter examined by the Committee arises out of the scrutiny of concerned Rules/Regulations
relating to the subject along with the Government’s comments received thereon.  The Committees’
observations/recommendations are contained in the Report that follows.
 
 
 
DIPANKAR   MUKHERJEE
Chairman
NEW DELHI                                                                                                                                            Committee on Subordinate Legislation,
February 11, 2002                                                                                                                                                                                  Rajya Sabha
                                         
                                                                                               
Report
 
I
 
Ministry of Finance Notification S.O. No. 995(E) dated 3rd November, 2000 regarding approval of GIC as Indian
Reinsurer under section 101A(8)(ii) of the Insurance Act, 1938-Implementation of 134th Report of the Committee on
Subordinate Legislation, Rajya Sabha.
 
      The Committee in its 134th Report presented to the House on 25th April, 2001 inter-alia dealt with the matter relating to Notification S. O. No.
995 (E) dated 3rd November 2000 issued by the Ministry of Finance (Annexure I) which had effect of restricting activities of the GIC in the area of
reinsurance only without formally amending the General Insurance Business (Nationalization) Act, 1972.  The Committee after examining the
subject matter observed as follows:
 
“that issue of notification S.O. 995(E) dated 3rd November 2000 which has the effect of restricting the activates of
GIC to the area of reinsurance, without   formally amending the parent Act was not a well considered course of
action on the part of the Ministry of Finance. In Committee’s views, the reasons advanced by the Ministry of
Finance that it is a requirement of law and the IRDA was insisting upon the issue are not convincing enough for
action in such a manner by the Ministry. The Committee is of the view that issue of notification before formally
amending the parent Act was putting the cart before the horse. The Committee also observed that the objectives of
Bill to entrust the task of Indian reinsurer to General Insurance Corporation and delink General Insurance
Corporation from its subsidiaries by carrying out necessary amendments in the GIBN Act 1972 as mentioned in the
Statement of Objects and Reason have already been brought into effect by the Ministry through the notification
followed by the administrative instructions of November 7, 2000. The effect of the notification was to take

140
file:///10.21.218.119/who%20am%20i/1%20rajesh%20sir/convert/english/Committee%20on%20Subordinate%20Legislation/140th.htm[25-10-2016 16:41:14]
advantage of a loophole in the Act to nullify the basic provisions of the Act, and in the Committee’s opinion  the 
action   and  the manner  in  which   it was  achieved constitutes an attempt to bypass the authority of Parliament.
That   this   was  realized   by   the   Ministry   is   clear  from  the subsequent introduction of a Bill on the same subject. The
Committee strongly deprecates the entire episode and trusts that Government will ensure that cases of this kind do not occur in future”.
 
2.     The fact that the General Insurance Business (Nationalization) Amendment Bill 2001 which was  introduced in the
Lok Sabha on 12.03.2001 was still pending gave an  impression as if the change in the role of GIC was being managed
by way of executive action or Administrative Instructions (Annexure II) without the authority of the Parliament.
Accordingly, the Committee considered the subject matter at its meeting held on Nov. 22, 2001 and as desired, the
Ministry of Finance was requested to furnish information as follows:
 “that the Committee on Subordinate Legislation, Rajya Sabha considered the subject matter in its meeting. While
the Committee noted that the General Insurance Business (Nationalization) Amendment Bill, 2001 which was
introduced in the Lok Sabha on the 12
th March 2001 is still pending, it desired to know precisely its present status
along with the present status with regard to the implementation of Ministry’s notification dated the 3 rd November
2000 approving GIC of India as the “Indian Reinsurer” as well as the instructions contained in their D.O. No.
8/27/200-Ins. VI dated 7.11.2000 addressed to the Chairman, GIC.”
 3.     In response, the Ministry of Finance (Insurance Division) vide  their O.M. dated December 3, 2001 furnished the
following:
 (i)       General Insurance Business (Nationalization) Bill, 2000 has been referred to the Standing Committee of Finance on 27 th August, 2001.  The
Bill is pending with the Standing Committee.  The Committee has already held a meeting with Associations and Unions of Insurance Companies.
(ii)     So far 16 insurance companies have been given certificate of registration by Insurance Regulatory & Development Authority.  All the
insurers are required to reinsure their business upto a certain percentage with GIC on its approval as Indian Reinsure on 3.11.2000.
 (iii)    After approval of GIC as the “Indian Re-insurer” four public sector general   insurance   companies   have  
been  given  operational  and functional autonomy on personnel, investment and re-insurance matters through an
administrative order on 7.1..2000.
              (iv)   To handle the co-ordination matter which was earlier handled by GIC a voluntary association of four public
sector general insurance companies namely General Insurers’ (Public Sector) Association of India has been
formed on the basis of recommendation of the Poddar Committee.
         (v)   GIPSA is a voluntary association of public sector general insurance companies.  Apart from co-ordination
matter, common problems concerns and issues of the four companies are discussed and debated in GIPSA forum for
a common approach.
 
4.     The Committee, not being satisfied with the information furnished by the Ministry of Finance, decided to hear their
representatives with a view to seek further clarifications/elucidations on the subject. Accordingly, the representatives of
the Ministry of Finance along with the representatives of the GIC appeared before the Committee on December 20,
2001. During the course of the oral evidence, the Committee desired to know the present status of the Notification dated
the 3rd November 2000 when the General Insurance Business Nationalization (Amendment) Bill, 2001 was still pending
with the Department Related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Finance. The Committee also wanted to know from
the representatives whether the amendment in the General Insurance Business Nationalization Act, 1972 was still
necessary or the Notification issued by the Ministry was enough and if the amendment in the Act was still necessary,
then how did Government issue the Notification. In other words, the Committee wanted a specific reply from the
representatives whether any further amendment of the GIBN Act was called for under the circumstances. The
Committee also wanted confirmation from the Ministry whether the Administrative Instructions dated 7
th November
2000 called for any Legislative backing. In response to the queries from the Committee, the Additional Secretary in-
charge of the Insurance Division in the Ministry of Finance while trying to clarify the position, referred to the enactment
of the Insurance (Regulation and Development) Authority Bill which came  into force with effect  from the 19 th April 
2000. Referring to this
 
Act, he stated that this Legislation had brought about significant changes in the Insurance Act, 1938 as well as the
General Insurance Business Nationalization  Act,  1972.  Earlier,  the  GIC  and  its  four  subsidiaries were
controlling the entire business of General Insurance. The four subsidiaries had the whole field of General Insurance for
competition amongst them. The situation underwent a change with the coming into the force of the IRDA Act which
resulted in opening up of the insurance sector in the private sector. Keeping in view these changes, the GIC which was a
reinsurer only in respect of the four companies had to assume the role of Reinsurer for the private companies also
coming up in the field and hence it was required that GIC be declared as a Reinsurer under section 101A (8)(ii) of the
Insurance Act, 1938. With a view to explain the basis on which Government had issued the Notification dated the 3
rd
November 2000 followed by Administrative Instructions of 7 th November 2000, the representatives stated that as per

140
file:///10.21.218.119/who%20am%20i/1%20rajesh%20sir/convert/english/Committee%20on%20Subordinate%20Legislation/140th.htm[25-10-2016 16:41:14]
the GIBN Act, the Central Government had powers to issue directions and in this context a reference was made to
Section 23 of the GIBN Act which reads out as follows:
 
“The Corporation and every acquiring company shall, in the discharge of its functions, be guided by such directions
in regard to matters of policy involving public interest as the Central Government may give.”
 
5.     The Committee was, however, not satisfied with the explanation furnished by the representatives of the Ministry of
Finance with regard to the basis on which they had issued the Notification as well as the Administrative Instructions
dated the 3rd and 7th November, 2000, respectively. The Committee’s feeling was that the action taken by Government
through the said Notification and the Administrative Instructions ran contrary to the provisions of the General Insurance
Business Nationalization Act, 1972 an amendment to which was still under consideration of the Department Related
Committee on Finance. The representatives of the Ministry agreed to furnish a note clarifying the position. The
Committee also directed the representatives to apprise the Standing Committee on Finance of the recommendations of
COPU as well as this Committee on the subject which is presently ceased of the matter.
 
6.        The Ministry of Finance vide their communication dated 11 th January 2002 furnished their action taken report on the 134 th Report of the
Committee on  the subject  along with  reply to  the observations  made by  the Committee
 
 
during the course of the oral evidence on December 20, 2001. The action taken report as received is enclosed (Annexure
III).
 
7.     The Committee notes with satisfaction that the Ministry of Finance has since forwarded the recommendations of
the COPU as well as this Committee (as contained in the 134
th Report) to the Standing Committee on Finance which it
feels would facilitate better consideration of the matter by them.
 
8.        The Committee is not convinced by the comments furnished by the Ministry of Finance with regard to the basis on
which they had issued the Notification dated the 3 rd November 2000 under Section 101A(8)(ii) of the Insurance Act,
1938 as well as the Administrative Instructions dated 7 th November 2000 under Section 23 of the GIBN Act, 1972 with
a view to restrict the activities of GIC to reinsurance business and give operational and functional autonomy to four
subsidiaries in matters relating to reinsurance, investment and personnel. The Committee is not satisfied with the
correlation sought to be established by the Ministry among sections 2(7A)(c), 101A(8)(ii) of the Insurance Act, 1938
and sections 25 and 23 of the GIBN Act, 1972 for the purpose of justifying the basis for the issue of the Notification as
well as the Administrative Instructions. The Committee still feels that the action of the Ministry of Finance, Insurance
Division, declaring GIC as the Indian Reinsurer as well as grant of operational and functional autonomy to the
subsidiaries through Administrative Instructions runs contrary to the provisions of the General Business Nationalization
Act, 1972 as it stands at present. This is evident from the perusal of the General Insurance Business Nationalization
(Amendment) Bill, 2001, which is presently under consideration of the Standing Committee on Finance, Section 9(1) of
the General Business Nationalization Act, 1972 contemplates the role of “superintending, controlling and carrying on
business of general insurance” for the GIC which is sought to be changed to “carrying on reinsurance business” through
the said Amendment Bill. The Committee is unable to understand how the change effected in the role of the GIC can get
alongwith the provisions of the GIBN Act, 1972 until the amendment is carried out.The proposed insertion of a new
section 24(A) in the GIBN Act, 1972 whereby the corporation has, on and from the commencement of the General
Insurance Business Nationalization Amendment Act, 2001, been made to cease to carry on general insurance business
also establishes that certain amendments were called for in the GIBN Act before the Government could effect the
changes in
 
the role and function of the GIC. Now, when the General Insurance Business Nationalization (Amendment) Bill, 2001 is
presently under consideration of the Standing Committee on Finance, the Committee recommends that the Ministry of
Finance should not implement their notification dated 3
rd November 2000 as well as the Administrative Instructions
dated 7th November 2000 till the GIBNA Bill as introduced in the Parliament is passed.

NOTIFICATION
 
New Delhi 3rd November, 2000
 
 
      S.O. 995(E) In exercise of the power vested with the Central Government under Secretion 101A (8)(ii) of the
Insurance Act, 1938, the Central Government hereby approves General Insurance Corporation of India as the “Indian
Reinsurer” to carry on reinsurance business in India.
 
Annexure-II
 
D.O.No.8/27/200-Ins.VI dated 7.11.2000 addressed to Shri D. Sengupta
Chairman, G.I.C. of India from Shri Ajit M. Sharan, Joint Secretary
(INS), Ministry of Finance, Department of Economic Affairs.
 
        In has been decided by the Government that the General Insurance Corporation of India (GIC) shall be the “Indian
Re-insurer” under Section 101 (A) (8) (ii) of the Insurance Act, 1938.  This Section provides that-
 
        “Indian re-insurer” means an insurer specified in sub-clause (b) of clause (9)  of Section 2  who carries on
exclusively re-insurance business and is approved in this behalf by the Central Government.”
 
2.     As per requirements of the above Section, GIC will now have to restrict itself exclusively to  re-insurance business
and should cease doing direct insurance business. Presently GIC is carrying on direct business in the areas of  aviation
and crop insurance.  It also supervises and controls the four subsidiary companies in relation to the conduct of general
insurance business GIC may, henceforth, cease underwriting direct aviation and crop insurance business.   These
businesses may now be underwritten by the subsidiary companies in line with the recommendations of the Poddar 
Committee.
 
3.     GIC may take action to implement the other recommendations of the Poddar Committee to give operational and
functional autonomy to the four subsidiary companies in the following areas:
 
·
     Personnel matter
·     Investments
·     Reinsurance
 
4.     A General insurers’ (Public Sector) Association of India (GIPSA) may also be constituted as suggested by the
Poddar Committee to effect coordination among the four subsidiary companies.  This Association may be entrusted with
coordination in the areas of personnel, technical reinsurance, investment and other matters as recommended by the
Poddar Committee.
 
Annexure-II
 
 
Committee on Subordinate Legislation – 134
th Report presented on 25.04.2001
 
        Observation & Recommendation
 
        The Committee considered the subject at its meeting held on 9
th April, 2001 and observed that issue of notification
S.O. 995(E) dated 3rd November 2000 which has the effect of restricting the activities of GIC to the area of reinsurance,
without formally amending the parent Act was not a well considered course of action on the part of Ministry of
Finance.  In Committee’s view, the reasons advanced by the Ministry of Finance that it is a requirement of law and the

140

IRDA was insisting upon the issue are not convincing enough for action in such a manner by the Ministry.  The
Committee is of the view that issue of notification before formally amending the parent Act was putting  the cart before
the horse.   The Committee also observed that the objectives of Bill to entrust the task of Indian reinsurer to General
Insurance Corporation and delink  General Insurance Corporation from its subsidiaries by carrying out necessary
amendments in the GIBNA Act 1972 as mentioned in the Statement of Objects and Reasons have already been brought
into effect by the Ministry through  the notification followed by the administrative instructions of November 7, 2000. 
   The effect of the notification was to take advantage of  a loophole in the Act to nullify the basic provision  of the Act,
and in the Committee’s opinion the action and the manner in which it was achieved constitutes an attempt to bypass the
authority of Parliament.  That this was realized by the Ministry is clear from the subsequent introduction of the Bill on
the same subject.  The  Committee strongly deprecates the entire episode and trusts that Government will ensure that
cases of this kind do not occur in future.
 
        Reply of the Government
 
        Government issued notification dated 3.11.2000 through existing power vested  under section 101A(8)(ii)  of
Insurance  Act 1935.   The  legal position and the circumstances under which the notification issued are given in the
following paragraph:
 
·     Vide notification No.S.O.770 (E) dated 29
th December, 1972 issued under Section 35 of the General Insurance
Business (Nationalisation)  Act, 1972, the concept  of  Indian Re-insurer defined in Section 101 A (8)(ii) of Insurance
Act, 1938 had been modified to mean General  Insurance Corporation (GIC). Thus in nationalized scenario, Indian Re-
insurer meant GIC which was taking care of the reinsurance business of its four subsidiaries.
 
·     With the enactment of Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority (IRDA) Act, 1999, the monopoly of the
nationalized insurance industry ceased and private insurance companies started getting registration from IRDA for
commencing insurance business in India.  GIC, therefore, could not have reinsured the business of private insurance
companies.
 
·     For reinsuring the business of private insurance companies, it was required to be notified as “Indian Reinsurer”
under Section 101A(8)(ii) Insurance Act, 1938.
 
·     Therefore, the notification issued under Section 35 of GIBNA 1972 was rescinded and GIC was approved on
3.11.2000 as “Indian Reinsurer” under Section 101A(8)(ii) of Insurance Act, 1938.  Which is an existing Ligislation.
 
2.     As per Section2(7A)(c) of the Insurance Act, 1938 an “Indian insurance company” can carry on life insurance
business or general insurance business or re-insurance business. Further, Section 101A(8)(ii) of the Insurance Act, 1938,
provides that an “Indian re-insurer” is to restrict itself exclusively to reinsurance business. Under Section 23 of GIBNA
1972, GIC and the subsidiary companies are under obligation to be guided by direction in regard to matters of policy 
involving public interest as the Central Government may give.  Since it was decided as a matter of policy to declare GIC
as the “Indian Re-insurer” and necessary notification issued, keeping in view the above referred legal position,
directions were issued to GIC on 7.11.2000 to restrict its activities reinsurance bossiness and give operational and 
functional autonomy to four subsidiaries on matters relating to re-insurance, investment and personnel.
 
3.     As regards amendment to the GIBNA, 1972 it is clarified that its main purpose was to delink  GIC from its

3. Point referred 
 Regulation 13: Proviso 
  
Provided that the Executive Committee may of its own 
motion review any such decision and where it reviews any such 
decision, it shall give an opportunity to the officer conc erned 
to make his representation in the matter. 
 
i) What is the criteria for reviewing the decision of 
the Committee by the Executive Committee?  Whether it is 
done regularly or in exceptional cases? 
 
ii) Clause (3) of regulation 13 states that the 
decision of the Committee shall be final, whereas the proviso 
to clause (3) empowers the Executive Committee to review the 
decision of the Committee.  There appears to be contradiction.  
Please elucidate. 
 
Comments  of the Bank 
 
i) The decision, if any, given by the Committee is 
not in consonance with the principles of natural justice, such 
matters if brought to the notice of the Executive Committee by 
the Bank the Executive Committee can review the decision of 

the C ommittee appointed for redressal of anomalies.  
However,  there was no occasion to review the decisions  of the 
Committee, as the cases of anomalies brought to the notice of 
the Committee were taken up with State Bank of India, 
Central Office who in turn h ad taken up with appropriate 
authorities viz., IBA and as per the clarification given by them 
the fitment appeal have been disposed off. 
 
ii) As far as the aggrieved officer is concerned, the 
decision of the Committee is final and he cannot appeal to 
Executive Committee for review of the decision of the 
Committee. However, the Executive Committee, suo motto can 
review the decision of the Committee and in such a review shall 
give an opportunity to the officer to represent his case.  In a 
limited sense, we may sa y, the decision of the Committee is 
subject to review by the Executive Committee. 
 
4. Point referred 
Regulation 15                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
 
(3) Any other person appointed to any gr ade including 
Junior Management Grade shall be on probation for such 
period as may be decided by the competent authority. 
 
Provided that the competent authority may, in the case 
of any officer, reduce or dispense with the  period of 
probation. 
 
  This regulation gives blanket power to competent 
authority to decide the period of probation, which might be 
misused.  Whether the Ministry have issued any  guidelines 
to the competent authority?  If so, the details thereof? 
 
Comments of the Bank 
 

 This is  only an enabling provision, to equip the 
competent authority with the powers to reduce or dispense 
with the period of probation, in case of direct appointment in 
senior position, where such probation period of longer 
duration may not be required by virtue  of his experience in 
discharging similar duties.  However, in practice, the authority 
conferred under this regulation is not exercised.  As a part of 
promotional policies every officer is kept on one year 
probation on promotion from one grade to another right upto 
scale VII.  In this connection, no guidelines have been received 
from the Ministry. 
 
 
4.1 Point referred  
Regulation 15: Proviso 
 
This proviso creates disparity among the Bank  Officers 
and directly affects the spirit of equality under article 14 of the 
Indian Constitution.  Whether the Ministry have any objection 
to specify the conditions under which the probation period of 
a particular officer will be reduced or dispensed with? 
 
Comments of the Bank 
 
  Probationary Officers who are entering the  Bank’s  
service for the first time have to be adequately trained 
before they are entrusted with responsible assignments.  
Similarly Trainee Officers (Group  B Officers)  considering 
their limited exposure to various spheres of banking 
activity are also pu t under training for a   period of one 
year.  Taking into account the nature of appointment of 
these category of officers, the probation period has been  
prescribed as two years as against one year for other 
promoted officers.  Even though probation period  has  
prescribed  as two years and one year for probationary 

officers, Trainee Officers and one year for other  
promotees respectively  for all purposes viz., increment, 
seniority, and promotion it is their date of 
appointment/date of promotion which are t aken into 
account and not the date of confirmation,  for determining 
their consequential benefits.  Therefore, fixation of 
different probation period for different category of officers 
is related to needs of training/job requirements and does 
not amount to  violation of Article 14 of the Constitution. 
 
5. Point referred 
       Regulation 19 
 
(1) An officer shall retire from the service of the  Bank on 
attaining the age of fifty eight years or upon the completion of 
thirty years’ service whichever occurs first. 
 
Provided that the Competent Authority may, at its 
discretion extend the  period of service of an officer who has 
attained the age of fifty eight years or has completed thirty 
years’ service as the case may be, should such extension be 
deemed desirable in the interest of the Bank. 
 
Provided further that an officer who had joined the 
service of the Bank either as an officer or otherwise on or after 
the 19th July, 1969 and attained the age of 58 years shall not be 
granted any  further extension in service. 
 
Provided further that an officer may, at the discretion 
of the Executive Committee, be retired from the Bank’s service 
after he has attained 50 years of age or has completed 25 years’ 
service, as the case may be, by giving him three months’ notice 
in writing or pay in lieu thereof. 
 

Provided further that an officer who has completed  25 
years’ service may be permitted by the Executive Committee 
to retire from the Bank’s service, subject to his giving three 
months notice in writing or pay in lieu thereof unl ess this 
requirement is wholly or partly waived. 
 
Under what circumstances an officer may be 
compulsorily retired?  Whether, principles of natural justice 
is followed in doing so? 
 
Comments  of the Bank 
 
  This regulation in principle provides an opportunity to 
review service records and performance of an officer based 
upon which the extension in his service could be considered 
on completing 25 years of service or attaining 50 years of 
age.  However, in practice first such review is being made 
only on attai ning 50 years of age or   on completion of 30 
years of service whichever is earlier in case of those joined 
the services of the Bank after 19.7.69 and 55 years of age 
or 30 years of service whichever is earlier in case of those 
joined before 19.7.1969.  Si milarly, second such review is 
being done on attaining 55/58 years of age depending upon 
their date of joining the service of the Bank.  In case the 
service records and performance report of the officer is not 
satisfactory, he will be given an extension fo r a shorter 
period, and also advised to improve upon deficient areas of 
his performance.  Depending upon his subsequent 
performance, further extension will be considered.  The 
very fact that the discretion to retire the officer at the end 
of 25 years of service or on attaining 50 years is vested with 
the Executive Committee, the highest decision making 
body in the Bank who represent various interests including 
those officers and workmen and does so after 
independently applying their minds, ensures that the  

principles of natural justice are upheld.  Further, no courts 
have so far questioned the powers under the  principles of 
natural justice.

 As per regulations “Pay” means basic pay including

 Letter No.1/33/81-Vigilance dated 29.6.81 issued by the 
Ministry of Finance Department of Economic Affairs 
(Banking Division) to the Chairman & Managing Director of 
the nationalized banks.  
 
Subject:  Suspension of officials of public sector 
banks - periodic review of their cases 
(Guidelines) 
   
Sir, 
 
 I am directed to say that several cases have come to the 
notice of the Government where the bank officials facing 
departmental/criminal proceedings have been kept under 
suspension for excessively long periods.  Though suspension is 
not a punishment, it certainly constitutes a great hardship  for 
the  concerned official. In fairness to him it is necessary   that 
the pe riod of suspension should conform to the barest 
minimum.  In this context the following instructions are 
reiterated for guidance and strict compliance:- 
 
(a) An official may generally be placed under suspension 
only in the following circumstances:- 
 
(i) where the continuance in office of the official 
will lead to prejudice investigation, trial or any 
inquiry (e.g. apprehended tampering with 
witnesses or documents); 
 
(ii) where the continuance in  office of the official is 
likely to seriously subvert discipline in the office 
in which he is working; 

 
(iii) where the continuance in office of the official 
will be against, wider  public interest, e.g. if 
there is a public scandal and it is considered 
necessary to place the official under suspension 
to demonstrate the policy of the bank to deal 
strictly with officers involved in such scandals,  
particularly  corruption. 
 
(iv) where preliminary, enquiry into allegations 
made has revealed a prima facie case justifying 
criminal or departmental proceedings which are 
likely to lead to his conv iction and or dismissal 
removal or compulsory retirement from  
service;  and  
 
(v) where the official is suspected to have engaged 
himself in activities prejudicial  to the interest of 
the security of the state. 
 
(b) Even in the above circumstance, an official may  be 
placed under suspension only in respect of misdemeanor of the 
following type: 
 
(i) an offence of conduct involving moral turpitude. 
 
(ii) corruption, embezzlement or misappropriation 
bank money, possession of disproportionate 
assets, misuse of official power of personal 
gains; 
 
(iii) services abandonment of official duty causing 
great loss to the Bank. 
 
(iv) Flight from duty; and  

 
(v) “refusals or caliberate failure to carry out 
written orders of supervisory officers. 
 
(c) While placing an official under suspension the 
competent authority should consider whether the 
purpose cannot be served by transferring the official 
from his post  to a post where be may not repeat the 
misconduct or influence the investigations, i f any, in 
progress.  If the authority finds that the purpose cannot 
be served by transferring the official from his post to 
another post then he should record reasons therefore, 
before placing the official under suspension. 
 
(d) In case where an official is deemed to have been placed 
under suspension under Discipline and Appeal 
Regulations etc, as soon as the official is released from 
the police custody the competent authority should 
consider the case to decide whether the continuance of 
the official under suspension is absolutely necessary or 
not.  If the period of suspension has already exceeded 
the limit of three months and the competent authority 
does not find justification to revoke the suspension in 
such  case he should immediately make a report to the 
next higher authority giving detailed justification for 
continuing the official under suspension. 
 
(e) In order keep the period of suspension to the barest 
minimum the competent authority should take all 
possible steps to file a charge sheet in a court of law, 
where an official has been placed under suspension on 
account of a court case or serve the chargesheet if the 
action is to be taken under the Discipline and Appeal 
Regulations within three months from the date of 
suspension and in case it is not possible to do so to 

report the matter to higher authorities explaining  the 
reasons for delay. 
 
(f) In respect of cases other than those pending in courts, 
the total period of suspension should not ordinarily 
exceed six months except in exceptional cases where it 
is not possible to adhere to this time limit then the 
competent authority should make a report to the next 
higher authority exploring the reasons for delay. 
 
(g) All authorities receiving information/report about the 
continued suspension of officials from their 
subordinate authorities should carefully examine each 
case and see whether the continued suspension of an 
official is absolutely necessary or the suspension should 
be revoked by transferring the official to another post 
of office. 
 
In order to ensure that the above instructions are 
scrupulously observed by subordinate authorities; all cases of 
suspension may please be reviewed regularly, at intervals of 
six months, particularly those where officials are under 
suspension  for more than six months, and wherever it is 
found that the official can be allowed to resume duties by 
transferring him from his post to another post and where 
necessary in consultation with CBI/CID/Police or other 
appreciate agencies, order  should be issued for revoking the 
suspension and allowing the official to resume duties with 
further direction as may be considered desirable in each 
individual case.  The review should not, however, be done in 
a repressed way and it should be borne in mind that 
revocation of suspension does not prejudice the criminal or 
Departmental Proceedings.

Committee’s Observation 
 
As regards framing of Regulations under section 52, the

Whether the Regulations as required under Section 52 
(3) have been laid on the Table of both Houses of Parliament, 
if so; the details thereof?

 SIDBI General Regulations, 1990, SIDBI (Issue and 
Management of Bonds) Regulations, 1990 and SIDBI 

(Employees Provident Fund) Regulations, 1990 have been laid 
on the Table of both the Houses of Parliament on 5 th August, 
1991. 
 
Committee’s Observation 
 
 The Committee noted that various Regulations framed 
under Small Industries Development Bank of India Act, 1999 
have been laid on the Table of both the Houses of Parliament 
on the 5th August, 1991. 
 
V. Point referred Section 54 
 
“If any difficulty arises in g iving effect to the 
provisions of this Act, the Central Government 
may, in consultation with the Development 
Bank, by order, do anything, not inconsistent

Whether any Orders have been issued under the

 There was no occasion for issue of any order under

The Committee noted the reply furnished by the 
Ministry regarding removal of difficulties under Section 54.

VII 
Banking Service Commission Act, 1984-Delay in framing of 
Rules/Regulations 
 
 
 The Banking Service Commission  Act was enacted in 
the year 1984.  But till date, the Act has not been enforced by 
the Ministry of Finance.  The Committee on Subordinate 
Legislation, Rajya Sabha which dealt with the subject and in 
its 101 st Report presented to the House on 26 th April, 1 994 
inter-alia examined the aspect of delay in framing of 
rules/regulation under the said Act.  The Committee’s 
observations/recommendations as contained in its 101st Report 
are reproduced below: 
 
“2.10 The Committee notes with deep concern the fact 
that the Banking Service Commission Act, 1984 
has not been enforced even after more than 9 
years. 
 
2.11 The Committee takes serious view of the fact 
that the Ministry have given a routine and even 
contradictory information.   On the one hand, 
they intimated that “act ion has already been 
initiated for setting up of the Banking Service 
Commission and for framing rules under 
Section 31 of the Act” which was further 
supplemented that “the question of appointment 
of Chairman and members of the Commission 
after which the Act would be brought into force 
is under consideration at the highest level in the 
Government”. On the other hand the Ministry, 
subsequently intimated that “the question 
whether the Act should be got repealed or 

continue to be held in abeyance is engaging th e 
attention of the Government”.  The Committee 
feels that the Ministry owes an explanation for 
this. 
 
2.12 The Committee is of the considered view that 
though the timing of giving effect to an Act of 
Parliament is the discretion of the 
Administrative Ministry, it is, however, not the 
intention of Parliament that the Government 
should keep an Act passed by both the Houses of 
Parliament and assented to by the President, in 
limbo for such a long time. 
2.13 The Committee is constrained to observe that 
while the Government has shown great alacrity 
in getting the Bill passed by the Parliament, it is 
strange that the Government drags its feet in the 
implementation of the Act. 
 
2.14 The Committee, therefore, recommends that 
after reviewing the matter either the Act be 
enforced or be got repealed within a period of 
six months and the Committee be informed, 
accordingly.  The Committee is not inclined to 
grant any further extension of time in this 
regard.

3. In 1996 the Mehta Committee had submitted its Report

norms etc.  Besides, in the context of technological up -
gradation, there would be need to reassess the

 “The proposal for abolition of the Banking Service 
Recruitment Boards is under examination and 
modalities for implementing the same are in process in 
consultation with Reserve Bank of India/Indian Banks 
Association.  After the action on this issue is complete 
Government will consider the question of repealing or 
retention of the Banking Service Commission Act, 
1984, the process is expected to get completed by July 
2001”. 
  
8. The Committee notes that the Ministry of Finance have 
in the meantime introduced a Bill in Lok Sabha in March, 2002  
with the objective of repealing the Banking Service 
Commission Act 1984.  The Committee, however, feels that lot 
of time has elapsed even after the introduction of the Bill.  The

expedite their action in the matter.  
 
VIII 
 
SUMMARY OF RECOMMENDATIONS

The Ministry vide their O. M. dated December 3, 2001

The Canara Bank/Punjab National Bank (Officers’)

The Committee notes with satisfaction that the

The Committee notes with satisfaction that the

VI 
The Small Industries Development Bank of India 
Act,1989-Framing of Regulations Under the 
 
 
The Ministry of Finance, Department of Economic

forwarded a copy of notification dated 16. 02. 2001 on Small 

Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) Employees’

Banking Service Commission Act, 1984-Delay in framing of

8. The Committee notes that the Ministry of Finance

Report 
  
I 
Laying of Statutory Orders on the Table of  Rajya Sabha 
  
  
            During the 195th Session of the Rajya Sabha, 267 Statutory Orders were laid 
on the Table of the House by the various Ministries/Departments.   The details of the 
Gazette Notifications in which these were published & the date of their laying on th e 
Table of the Rajya Sabha have been indicted in the enclosed Ministry wise statement 
(Annexure). 
  
2.         During the course of general scrutiny of these Orders, the Committee has 
noted some cases where there has been a considerable time lag between th e date of 
notification of the Order and the date of its laying. The annexed statement also 
indicates the period of delay in cases where notifications have not been laid as per the 
Committee’s guidelines.  In some of the cases the delay has been quite abnormal.  The 
observations/ recommendations of the Committee respect of specific 
Ministries/Departments are as follows:- 
             
i.         Ministry of Commerce & Industry  
The Committee notes that the Ministry of Commerce and Industry have laid 
on the Table of the Rajya Sabha the Tobacco Board (Recruitment) Regulations, 1984 
as well as the Tobacco Board (Recruitment) Regulations, 1989 just because it was not 
possible for them to confirm beyond doubt whether these regulations had been laid 

before both House of Parliament earlier as the relevant records were not traceable. 
The Committee, while it appreciates the initiative of the Ministry, but, at the same 
time, it expects them to set right their records relating to the framing and the laying 
of subordinate legislation under various Acts being administered by them at-least for 
future so that such situations are avoided. 
  
ii.         Ministry of Communication and Information Technology 
            The Committee regrets to find that out of the five notifications laid by the 
Ministry of Communication and Information Technology, there has been a delay in 
case of two (sl. nos. 27 and 28 of the Annexure). The Committee expects the Ministry 
of Communication, etc. to exercise caution in such matters for future and ensure that 
the schedule as prescribed by the Committee in the matter of laying of subordinate 
legislation framed under various Acts of Parliament is followed meticulously from 
time to time. 
  
iii.        Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution 
                        The Committee regrets to note that out of 15 notifications, there has 
been a delay in laying of seven as mentioned at sl. Nos. 4,5,6,9,10, 11 and 17A of the 
Annexure. The Committee would like the Ministry of Consume r Affairs, etc. to take 
steps to avoid recurrence of such instances and ensure the compliance of the schedule 
as laid down by the Committee in the matter of laying of rules/regulations, etc. in its 
131st and 135th Reports. 
  
iv.        Ministry of Finance 
                        The Committee deeply regrets to note that for the sixth consecutive 
Session, the Ministry of Finance is coming under its particular notice due to delay in 
the laying of subordinate legislation on the Table of the Rajya Sabha. Ironic ally, the 
magnitude of the default is larger this time. The Ministry have laid 184 
rules/regulations during the 195th Session and there has been delay in case of 141 (sl. 
nos. 34, 37 39 -80, 94 -130, 135 -160, 172, 173,174, 176 -197 and 226 -227 of the 
Annexure). The Committee is even further pained to note the period by which the 
laying has been delayed which roughly averages anywhere between 8 –12 months. In 

the opinion of the Committee, calls for immediate corrective action. The Committee 
directs the Ministry of Finance to take action to prevent such lapses in the future. 
  
v.         Ministry of Home Affairs 
                        The Committee notes with regret that out of the seven notifications laid 
by the Ministry of Home Affairs during the 195 th Session, there has been a delay in 
case of five. In case of the Central Industrial Security Force Group “A” and   “B” 
Civilian Gazetted Posts Recruitment Rules, 2000, the delay is as long as of eleven 
months. The Committee would like the Ministry of Home Affairs to have a relook into 
the internal mechanism in place so as to obviate such instances for the future. 
  
vi.        Ministry of Information & Broadcasting 
The Committee notes with regret that there has been a delay of 1 year and 2 
months on the part of Minist ry of Information & Broadcasting in laying their only 
notification, namely, the Prasar Bharati (Broadcasting Corporation of India) 
(Audience Research Posts) Service Regulations (Sl. No. 245). 
             
The Committee hopes that the Ministry of Information & Broadcasting would 
take due care & ensure prompt compliance of the schedule prescribed by the 
Committee for the purpose. 
  
vii.       Ministry of Labour 
                        The Committee notes with regret that the Ministry of Labour have laid 
two notifications during the 195th Session and there has been a delay in both the cases. 
The Ministry could have laid both the notifications during the 194 th (Winter Session 
2001) of the Rajya Sabha, but they failed to do so. The Committee hopes that they 
would take necessary action and avoid such instances. 
                          
viii.      Ministry of Shipping 
The Committee regrets to note that the Ministry of Shipping has laid five 
notifications during the 195th Session and three out of them were delayed by a period 
ranging from 4-8 months. The Committee expects the Ministry to take necessary and 

corrective action in order to ensure that such delays do not recur and the schedule as 
prescribed by the Committee in the matter of laying of subordinate legislati on is 
followed, strictly.  
  
3.         Besides the above, the Committee also notes with regret the isolated cases of 
delayed laying of notifications by the Ministry of Human Resource Development (sl. 
no. 36 of the Annexure), Ministry of Law, Justice and Company Affairs (sl. no. 249 of 
the Annexure), Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (sl. no. 258 of the 
Annexure) and Ministry of Textiles (sl. no. 258 of the Annexure). The Committee 
would like these  Ministries to take note of the time schedule which is  reproduced 
hereinafter and ensure that the same is complied with meticulously for future. The 
Committee, accordingly, reiterates its observations made in its 135th Report : 
  
 “ The Committee has, time and again, emphasized that it is essential 
that in case there is a delay in the laying of Statutory Orders, the 
concerned Ministry/Department should invariably append a delay 
statement along with the notifications being laid so as t o apprise the 
Parliament of the causes of delay.   The Committee desires all 
Ministries/Departments to take a note of this, since the intention is that 
through the process of formulation of a delay statement the Ministry is 
able to introspect, identifying b ottlenecks and devising remedial 
measures”.   
  
4.         The Committee impresses again upon all the Ministries/Departments to follow 
the time schedule for laying as prescribed by it in its 131st Report as reproduced below 
:- 
  
“Orders required to be laid  before the House should be laid   (i) if the 
House is not in Session, during the Session immediately following the 
date of publication of the Order in the Official Gazette and (ii) if the 
House is in Session, on the date of the publication of the Order, during 
its continuance and in case the time lag between the date of publication 
and the date of the closing of the Session is less than 15 clear days, 

before the expiry of the Session immediately following the said 
Session.  All the Ministries/Departments of  Government of India 
should henceforth comply with this schedule in the matter of laying of 
the orders issued under various Acts of Parliament on the Table of the 
Rajya Sabha.”

Ministries/Departments in la ying of the various rules/regulations before the

asked to appear before the Committee for clarifications.  
  
3.         During the course of discussion on the draft Report, there was also a mention 
about the delay in framing of the subordinate legislation under various Acts of 
Parliament. A view was expressed that there should be some definite criteria for 
ascertaining whether there has been a delay in framing of the rules/ regulations or 
not. While it was appreciated that the process of framing of subordinate legislations 
was t ime consuming and the time required for the purpose may vary from one 
legislation to another, but, there was a suggestion that the Ministries/Departments 
may also be required to indicate in the memorandum of delegated legislation 
appended to the Bill, whic h gives the areas which are contemplated to be covered 
through subordinate legislation, the approximate time which would be required for 
framing the subordinate legislation and any delay beyond this time limit could be 
pursued by the Committee as a case of  delay. The Committee desired this aspect to 
be examined. The Committee also desired the Secretariat to examine the cases where 
there has been an unusual delay in framing of the rules/regulations for its 
consideration. The draft 142nd Report was, thereafter, adopted.

NEW DELHI 
August 12, 2002 
A. VIJAYA RAGHAVAN 
Chairman 
 Committee on Subordinate Legislation, 
 Rajya Sabha 
  

  
 
REPORT 
  
I 
  
The Coffee Board General Provident Fund Rules, 1965 
  
            The Committee examined the Coffee Board General Provident Fund Rules, 1965 
and certain points were referred to the Ministry of Commerce & Industry (Department 
of Commerce) on June 21, 1999 for their comments/clarifications.  The subject matter 
was taken up for discussion with the representatives of the Coffee Board and the 
Ministry of Commerce & Industry at Bangalore on June 28, 1999.  The points referred 
and the comments/clarifications of the Ministry of Commerce & Industry alongwith the 
Committee’s observation are reproduced below. 
  
1.         Point referred 
  
Whether these Rules have been laid on the Table of the Rajya Sabha; if so, the details 
thereof, if not the reasons therefore? 
  
            Ministry’s Comments: 
  
These Rules would definitely have been laid on the Table of the Rajya Sabha.  However, 
since these Rules were framed 34 years ago, it is very difficult to locate records to 
authenticate our claim. 
            Committee’s Observation 
  
The Committee expressed its concern over the non-availability of dates of laying of the 
rules on the Table of the Houses of Parliament.  The representatives assured to revert 
back to Committee on the issue at their earliest. 
  
2.         Point  referred 
Rule 2(1)(g) 
  
            “Family means” 
  
In the case of a male subscriber, the wife or wives and children of  a  subscriber  and 
the  widow, or widows, and  
children of the deceased son of a subscriber:  provided that if a subscriber proves that 
his wife has been judicially separated from him or has ceased under the customary law 
of the community to which  she belongs to be entitled  
to maintenance she shall henceforth be deemed to be no longer a member of the 
subscriber’s family in matter to which these rules relate unless the subscriber 
subsequently intimates in writing to the Accounts Officer that she shall continue to be so 
regarded; 
  
In the case of female subscriber, the husband and children of a subscriber and the 
widow or widows and children of a deceased son of a subscriber: provided that if a 
subscriber by notice in writing to the Accounts Officer expresses her desire to exclude 
her husband from her family, the husband shall henceforth be deemed to be no longer a 

member of the subscriber’s family in matter to which these rules relate unless the 
subscriber subsequently cancels such notice in writing: 
  
            Provisions in sub-clauses (i) & (ii) of clause (g) of sub-rules (1) of Rule 2 
prescribe different procedures in case of male and female employees of the Coffee 
Board for exclusion of spouse from the subscribers family. 
  
What is the justification for prescribing different procedures; whether Government 
have any objections in prescribing a uniform procedure for both male and female 
employees? 
 Ministry’s Comments 
  
            Since Coffee Board has adopted the Central Government General Provident 
Fund (Central Service) Rules, 1960 for the employees of the Coffee Board, the definition 
of family will be the same as the Central Government Employees.  Ministry of 
Commerce or Coffee Board are not competent to make any change  in the definition of 
family as these are based on  the  rules  framed  by  the   Government   of  India  in  the  
Department of Personnel which are applicable to all Central Government Employees. 
  
Committee’s Observation 
  
The Committee noted the reply. 
  
3.         Point referred 
            Rule 8(1) 
  
                        Conditions of subscriptions  
                         
“A subscriber shall subscribe monthly to the Fund except during  the period when he is 
under suspension;  
Provided that a subscriber may at his option, not subscribe during any period of leave, 
other than leave on average pay or earned leave of less than one month or 30 days 
duration, as the case may be;”   
  
As per the above proviso a subscriber may not subscribe to the Fund if he is on earned 
leave of a duration of more than 30 days or on some other leave.  What is the 
justification of keeping such a provision?  There is no such provision in the General 
Provident Fund rules applicable to Central Government Employees. 
Ministry’s Comments: 
  
            Though the provision was incorporated in the Coffee Board General Provident 
Fund Rules, 1965, in practice these provisions are not given effect to. 
  
            In fact Rule 28 of the Coffee Board General Provident Fund Rules, 1965, very 
clearly states that: 
  
“Notwithstanding the above provision, if the Central Government notify any change in 
the rate of subscription or modify  the  rules  and  procedures relating to advances  
and withdrawals in the General Provident Fund (Central Service) Rules, 1960, such 
change shall be made applicable to the servant of the Board also.” 
  

            With the aid of this enabling provision in the CBGPF Rules, 1965, the Board has 
been adopting all the changes made in the   Central PF Rules through the issue of 
relevant circulars.   The Board strictly follows the provisions of the General Provident 
Fund (Central Service) Rules, 1960. 
  
            Committee’s Observations 
  
The Committee was not satisfied with the Ministry’s reply and observed that when the 
proviso to Rule 8(1) has not been given effect to there is no justification for having such 
a provision in the Rule.  This proviso, therefore, should have been omitted from the 
Rules. 
  
4.         Point referred 
            Rule 9(1)(b) 
  
            Rates of subscription 
             
“The amount of subscription shall be fixed by the subscriber himself, subject to the 
following conditions, namely- 
  
It may be any sum, so expressed not less than 6 per cent of his emoluments and not 
more than his total emoluments; 
  
Provided that in the case of a subscriber who has previously been subscribing to the 
Board’s Contributory Provident Fund at the higher rate of 8 1/3  per cent, it may by 
any sum, so expressed, not less than 8 1/3 per cent, of his emoluments and not more 
than his total emoluments; 
  
Provided further that in case of class IV employees the minimum rate of subscription 
shall be Rs.4/- a month in the case of those drawing a pay of less than Rs.75/- a month 
and Rs.5/- a month in the case of others.” 
  
            The minimum amounts mentioned in the second proviso for class IV and other 
employees of the Board is very less.  Perhaps, these figures are based upon very old pay 
scale.  Whether the Ministry would inform when these limits were fixed; whether these 
limits are not due for revision and if so, by when these would be revised? 
             
            Ministry’s Comments: 
  
            It is submitted that the minimum subscription towards PF contribution by the 
Board employees has been fixed at the rate of 6% of the basic pay drawn by the 
respective officer/officials.  This procedure/practice has been in force in accordance 
with the General Provident Fund Rules and in accordance with the Rules 28 of Coffee 
Board General Provident Fund Rules. 
  
            Committee’s Observation 
  
The Committee was not satisfied with the reply and observed that when the second 
proviso to Rule 9(1) had not been given effect to there was no justification for having 
such a provision in the Rule.  This proviso, therefore, should be omitted from the Rules. 
  
5.         Point referred 

        Rule 9(4) 
             
Rates of subscription 
  
                        XXX                            XXX                   XXX                          
                        XXX                            XXX                   XXX                                     XXX       
         XXX                    XXX                             
                         
“The amount of subscription so fixed may by enhanced or reduced once at any time 
during the course of a year;” 
                         
            According to the rule the amount of subscription may be enhanced or reduced 
once at any time during the course of a year. 
  
As per Rule 9(4) of the General Provident Fund (Central Service) Rules, 1960, the 
amount of subscription once fixed can be enhanced twice during the course of the 
year.  Whether there is any objection to amend the rule accordingly? 
  
Ministry’s Comments: 
  
            The Board is permitting the subscribers to enhance the subscription towards PF 
twice in a financial year and once in a year of reduction of  subscription.  The necessary 
modifications have not been formally included in the CBGPF Rules, 1965, only because 
the Rules have not been re-printed.  The subscription will never be allowed below 6% of 
the basis pay of the respective employees. 
  
            Committee’s Observation 
  
            The Committee was not satisfied with the reply and observed that necessary 
formal modifications in the Coffee Board rules have to be carried out to allow the 
subscribers to enhance the subscription towards Provident Fund twice in a year.  The 
Committee further observed that mere reprinting of these rules was not the solution. 
  
6.         Point referred 
Rule 13(1)(b) 
  
Advance from the Fund  
  
The Chairman or any other officer of the Board, not below the rank of an Assistant 
Coffee Marketing Officer, authorised by the Chairman, may sanction the payment to 
any subscriber if an advance consisting of a sum of whole rupees and  not exceeding 
in  amount  three months pay or  
half the amount standing to his credit in the Fund whichever is less, for one or more of 
the following purposes: 
  
XXX                XXX                  XXX                                                  
to meet the cost of higher education, including where necessary, the travelling expenses 
of the subscriber or any person actually dependent on him in the following cases, 
namely. 
  
(i)         for education outside India for an academic, technical, professional or 
vocational course beyond the High School stage: and 

  
for any medical, engineering or the technical or specialised   courses in India beyond the 
High School stage provide that the course of study is for not less than  three years. 
  
            What is the objective for prescribing that a course of study should not be of less 
than three years. Whether the Ministry have any objection to delete the words 
“provided that the course of study is not less than three years” as many of the technical 
courses are expensive and are of lesser duration.  (Question also applies to rule 
16(1)(a)). 
  
            Ministry’s Comments: 
  
            The provision of “not less than three years” is being followed as per Rule 12 (b) 
(ii) of the Central GPF Rules which also prescribes this minimum requirement of 
time.  For all purposes, the Board follows only the Central PF Rule.  The Coffee Board 
does not have the authority to alter this, as this is a decision,  which can be taken only 
by the Union Government. 
             
            This answer holds good for Rule 16(1)(a) also. 
             
            Committee’s Observation 
  
The Committee noted the reply 
  
Point referred 
Rule 16 
  
Withdrawals from the Fund 
  
“Subject to conditions specified herein, withdrawals may be sanctioned by the chairman 
at any time after the completion of twenty years of service (including broken periods of 
service, if any) of a subscriber or within ten years before the date of retirement on 
superannuating, whichever is earlier, from the amount standing for his credit in the 
fund, for one or more of the following purposes, namely”- 
  
            For the Central Government Employees’ there has been a modification in the 
condition for withdrawal wherein they have been allowed to withdraw after completing 
15 years of service.  Coffee Board is still carrying the condition of 20 years of service in 
this regard.  What is the justification that a provision which is for the benefit of the 
Employees and which has been introduced in the Central Government in year 1995 has 
not been incorporated in these regulation so far? 
  
Ministry’s Comments: 
  
            From 1995 and onwards withdrawal from the respective PF accounts are being 
allowed to those employees who have completed 15 years service.   Prior to 1995, final 
withdrawal used to be allowed to such of the employees who had completed 20 years 
service. 
             
            Committee’s Observation 
             

            The Committee observed that although the Coffee is extending all the benefit 
that are available in the General Provident Fund (Central Service) Rules applicable to 
the Central Government Employees yet they have not amended these  rules for the 
purpose.  The Committee desired that corresponding amendments be made in the rules. 
  
Point referred 
  
            In the case of GPF Rules applicable to Central Government Employees there has 
been relaxation in the grant of advances as well as withdrawal for purpose of various 
consumers durables.  Whether the Ministry have taken any action for incorporating 
similar provisions in these regulations if so, the details thereof, if not the reasons 
therefore? 
  
Ministry’s Comments: 
  
            PF advance/withdrawals are allowed to purchase consumer durables in 
accordance with the directions of the Government. 
  
            Committee’s Observation 
  
            The Committee observed in general that in relation to several matters, the Coffee 
Board has been implementing the existing provisions of the General Provident Fund 
Rules applicable in Government of India without formal amendments in their 
rules.  The Committee did not approve this dispensation and observed that Coffee 
Board should follow the Central Government rules by making consequent changes in 
their rules  which would be a proper course of action. 
  
The Relevant extracts from the study note (Annexure-I) on the Committee’s visit to 
Bangalore etc., from June 27 to July 3, 1999 were forwarded to the Ministry on 
September 21, 1999 for necessary action.  The Ministry vide their O. M. dated 
November 19, 1999 informed that Coffee Board  has  accepted the 
Committee’s  suggestion for inserting a  
new clause in the Coffee Rules 1955 to the effect that employee of Board shall be 
governed by General Provident Fund (Central Service) Rule 1960 instead of having a 
separate set of rules and the process of making necessary amendment to the Coffee 
Rules for inserting a new clause had been initiated by the Ministry. 
  
3.         Thereafter, the Ministry of Commerce & Industry, Department of Commerce 
vide their O. M. dated July 24, 2000 intimated as under. 
  
                        XXX                         XXX                           XXX                             
  
“The proposal for making necessary amendment to the Coffee Rules, 1955 for inserting 
a new clause was taken up with the Legislative Department However, Legislative 
Department is not agreeable to the proposal and has advised this Department for 
updating the existing Coffee Board’s General Provident Fund Rules, 
1965.  Accordingly, the process for amending the existing GPF Rules of the Board is 
under way.” 
  
4.         After some reminders and interim replies, the Ministry of Commerce & Industry 
vide their O. M. dated April 17, 2001 forwarded a copy of the Coffee Board General 

Provident Fund (Amendment) Rules, 2001(Annexure-II) carrying out the amendment in 
the rules as per the Committee’s suggestion. 
5.         The Committee notes with satisfaction that the Ministry have carried out 
necessary amendment in the rules in pursuance to the deliberations with the latter. The 
Committee notes Ministry’s comments on Rule 2(1)(g) regarding definition of the term 
“family” and on rule 13(1)(b) regarding withdrawal of advance from Fund.  As regards 
the date of laying of the rules on the Table of the House the Committee notes with regret 
that the Ministry have failed to gather the desired information.  The Ministry should 
strive for a better  record management system in order to avoid such instances.   
The Committee, however, notes that the Ministry have laid the rules again on the 20th 
March, 2001 in order to cover up the prevailing uncertainty.  The Committee is also 
satisfied to note that the Ministry have agreed to its suggestions and, accordingly, 
notified amendments in Rules 8(1) regarding conditions and rate of subscriptions, in 
Rule 9(1)(b) regarding rates of subscription by omitting its second proviso, in Rule 9(4) 
regarding enhancement and reduction in the amount of subscription during a calendar 
year, in Rule-16 regarding withdrawal from the Fund and the purposes for which 
withdrawal is allowed by making them consistent with the corresponding provisions of 
the GPF Rules applied to Central Government employees.

II 
  
The Merchant Shipping (Management of Safe Operation of Ships) Rules, 2000 
             
            The Merchant Shipping (Management for the Safe Operation of Ships) Rules, 
2000 framed under the Merchant Shipping Act, 1958 were examined and certain points 
were referred to the Ministry of Shipping for their comments/clarifications on 
December 22, 2000. The Ministry vide their communication dated February 6, 2001 had 
furnished their comments. The points referred to the Ministry and the 
comments/clarifications received thereon are as under:  
  
Point referred. 
  
The Rules have been framed under Section 457 of the Merchant Shipping Act, 
1958.  What are the reasons that Government did not have any set of rules on the 
subject for over 4 decades & in what manner Government had been regulating this area 
of activity; what factors necessitated Government to frame the said Rules, now? 
  
            Ministry’s reply 
  
            Safe operation of ships and pollution prevention (International Safety 
Management Code) vide IMO Resolution No. A 741(18) dated May 1994 was made 
mandatory by Chapter IX of SOLAS  Convention, and has come into force from 1st July 
1998 depending on the type and tonnage of ships.  This code applies to passenger ships, 
tankers, gas carriers and bulk carriers and high speed crafts not later than1st July 
1998.  
  
            This code shall apply to other cargo ships and mobile offshore crafts not later 
than 1st July 2002.  The purpose of this Code is to provide international standard for the 
safe management and operation of ships and for pollution prevention.  These aspects 
are already covered under parts IX & XIA of the Merchant Shipping Act and 
various  Certificates  were prescribed  for  various activities.   The same activities are 
now proposed to be conducted in a different form to enhance better management.

(j) “Designated person”  means a person ashore with direct access to the highest level of

pollution aspects of the operation of each ship.

provisions of these rules.  So much so that the words ‘Designated Person’ have not been 
used anywhere else but in the definition. What may the reasons be for defining a term 
which has not been used in the provisions of the rules.   
  
(ii) In Sub rule (u) the Director General of Shipping has been 
authorized  to  delegate  the  power  to  issue  the  ‘Safety  Management Certificate’  to

Rule 2 (j) it is agreed that the designated person has not been reflected anywhere in the

Group ‘A’ posts and, if so, what is the justification for having a separate provision 
prescribing the manner in which Group ‘A’ posts in the Authority may be filled up; 
what is the justification for giving final authority to the Central Government for 
deciding the manner in which any Group ‘A’ posts in the Authority may be filled up? 
Comments 
  
The Recruitment Rules to be notified will cover filling up of Group ‘A’ posts also.  The 
provision made in the Regulation is of general nature and the detailed method of 
recruitment’s, scales of pay, qualifications, etc. have been prescribed in the proposed 
Recruitment Rules. 
  
Section 32 sub-section (2)(d) and Section 33 sub-section (2)(b) of the Agricultural and 
Processed Food Products Export Development Authority Act, 1985 vests the Central 
Government with such Authority. 
             
            Committee’s observations 

  
Committee noted the reply 
  
Point referred 
  
Regulation 28(9)(f) 
  
The Authority may contract services, as deemed fit.  No contract 
appointments   of   more   than 6 months   duration and/or  having basic monthly 
remuneration of Rs. 1800/-or more shall be made without prior approval of the Central 
Government. 
  
            Whether the functional requirements of the Authority are being met 
satisfactorily in view of the powers conferred upon it to allow contract appointments on 
remuneration up to Rs.1800/-per month? Secondly,  what  does  the words ‘basic 
monthly remuneration”  
signify; generally, remuneration is the total payment receivable by a person for services 
rendered and it is not clear what objective is sought to be achieved for qualifying 
remuneration by using the word ‘basic’? Should, the limits ofremuneration up to which 
contract appointments could be given be not definite? 
  
Comments 
  
The amount of Rs.1800/-mentioned in Regulation 28(9)(f) has since been amended to be 
Rs. 6000/- vide Notification No. APEDA/SEC/GEN/30 dated 5th May 2000.  The amount 
of Rs.6000/- mentioned here is the limit of total remuneration upto which contract 
appointments could be made by the Authority.  The amount of Rs.6000/- is the total 
payment receivable by a person for services rendered.  The word ‘basic’ could be 
deleted. 
  
Committee’s observations 
  
The Committee noted that under Regulation 28(9)(f) the Ministry have agreed to delete 
the word ‘basic’ as observed by the Committee. 
  
The Committee  notes the comments of the Ministry on point no. 1,2,6,9, & 10. The 
Committee is satisfied that the Ministry have agreed to its suggestions on regulations 7 
(point-3) for raising minimum strength of the quorum from 8 to 10 Members, 
regulation 10 and 26 (point-4) for modifying the existing provision of “second or casting 
vote” available to the Chairman or the presiding Officer, regulation-11(2) (point-5) for 
deleting the word “effectual” which was a printing mistake, Regulation 15(2) (point-7) 
for defining the words “of a policy nature”, regulation-16 (point-8) for providing a time 
limit within which the Authority can review the decision of the Committee and 
regulation-28(9) (F) (point-11) by substituting the words “basic monthly remuneration” 
with  the words “monthly remuneration”.  
  
The Committee recommends to the Ministry of Commerce and Industry to carry out 
the above amendments in the regulations expeditiously under intimation to it. 
 
  
IV 
  

Jawaharlal Nehru Port Trust Employees (Pay and Allowances)     Regulation, 1997-
Implementation of 79th Report of the Committee 
  
The Committee had examined the Jawaharlal Nehru Port Trust Employees (Pay and 
Allowances)Regulations, 1997 and made certain observations/recommendations as 
contained in its 126th Report which was presented to the House on December 23, 
1999.  The recommendations made by the Committee are as follows: 
  
“The Committee expresses satisfaction that the Ministry of Surface Transport had 
agreed to amend regulations 4, 19(1) and 24 as per its suggestions.  As regards 
regulation 2(19) the Committee decided that the regulation may be retained in its 
existing form.  The Committee hopes that the Ministry of Surface Transport will notify 
the amendments to regulation 4, 19(1) and 24 expeditiously under intimation to it.” 
  
The extracts from the Report were forwarded to the Ministry of Shipping (then 
Ministry of Surface Transport) on January 28, 2000 for implementation.  The Ministry 
of Shipping vide their O.M. dated 28.7.2000  forwarded a copy  of the notification No. 
G.S.R. 724 (E) dated 27.10.1999 containing the amendment in respect of Regulation  4

After a couple of reminders the Ministry of Shipping vide their O.M. dated 27.6.2001 
forwarded a copy of the notification No. G.S.R. 443 (E) dated 21.6. 2001 containing 
amendment to the regulation 24 also. 
  
4.         The Committee expresses its satisfaction that the Ministry have amended 
regulation 4 (1) (a) (i) by deleting the words, “or rupees twenty five only, whichever is

SUMMARY OF RECOMMENDATIONS 
  
I 
  
The Coffee Board General Provident Fund Rules, 1965 
  
            The Committee notes with satisfaction that the Ministry have carried out

 Prescribing minimum level of the Officers for issuing   Safety Management Certificate
