INTRODUCTION 
  
      I, the Chairman of the Committee on Subordinate Legislation, having been authorized 
by the Committee to present the Report on its behalf, do hereby present this Hu ndred 
and Forty Fifth  Report of the Committee. 
. 
1.2  The Committee considered and adopted the Report in its meeting held 
on  December  9, 2002 
  
1.3  The notifications containing Rules/Regulations, etc. laid on the Table of the Rajya 
Sabha during its 196th session have been perused by the Committee in the light of 
the provisions of the Acts under which these were framed and also with a view to 
seeing whether these have been laid within the prescribed time -frame and 
properly.  The Committee’s observations/ recommendations are contained in the 
report that follows.  
  
  
NEW DELHI 
December 9, 2002 
A. VIJAYARAGHAVAN 
Chairman 
 Committee on Subordinate Legislation, 
Rajya Sabha 
  
  
 
 Report 
I 
Laying of Statutory Orders on the Table of  Rajya Sabha 
  
      During the 196 th Session of the Rajya Sabha, 78 Statutory Orders were laid on the 
Table of the House by the various Ministries/Departments.   The details of the Gazette 
Notifications in which these were published and the date of their laying on the Table of 
the Rajya Sabha have been indicated in the Ministry-wise statement placed at Annexure. 
  
2.   During the course of scrutiny of these Orders, the Comm ittee has noted some cases 
where there has been a considerable time lag between the date of notification of the Order 
and the date of its laying. The annexed statement also indicates the period of delay in 
cases where notifications have not been laid as pe r the Committee’s guidelines.  In some 
of the cases the delay has been quite abnormal.   The observations/ recommendations of 
the Committee in respect of specific Ministries/Departments are as follows: - 
  

I     Ministry of Commerce & Industry  
      The Committee notes that out of the five notifications laid by the Ministry of 
Commerce and Industry, there has been a delay in two cases (sl. nos. 6 and 7 
)  of  the  Annexure. The Ministry have also not enclosed the delay statement giving the 
reasons for  the delay in laying. The Committee expects the Ministry of Commerce & 
Industry to exercise caution in such matters and ensure that the   schedule as prescribed 
by the Committee in the matter of laying of Subordinate Legislation framed under 
various Acts of Parliament is followed meticulously in future . 
  
II    Ministry of Finance & Company Affairs 
  
      The Committee is unhappy over the fact that for the seventh consecutive session, 
the  Ministry  of Finance and Company Affairs are  
coming under its particular notice on account of delay in the laying of Subordinate 
Legislation on the Table of the Rajya Sabha. The Ministry have laid 30 rules/regulations 
during the 196 th Session and there has been delay in case of 27 ranging from 1 year 5 
months to 3 months as shown in the Annexure and in none of the cases, delay statement 
has been appended.  The Committee   recommends that the Ministry of Finance and 
Company Affairs  should take immediate corrective action and ensure that henceforth 
the subordinate legislation is laid before the Parliament on time. 
  
III  Ministry of Home Affairs 
  
      The Committee notes with regret that out of the eleven notifications laid by the 
Ministry of Home Affairs during the 196 th Session, there has been delay in case  of four 
(sl. nos. 54 to 56 and 58).   The Committee would like the Ministry to streamline its 
procedures so as to obviate such instances in future.  
  
IV  Ministry of Information & Broadcasting 
  
      The Committee notes with regret that there has been a delay of five months in laying 
two of the notifications (sl. nos. 61 and 63) and no delay statement was sent 
therewith.  The Committee hopes that the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting 
would take adequate steps to ensure compliance with the time sche dule as laid down by 
the Committee for the laying of Subordinate Legislation. 
  
V    Ministry of Law and Justice  
      The Committee notes with regret that there has been a delay of seven months on the 
part of the Ministry  of Law  and Justice  in laying   
their only   notification (sl. no. 64)   and  no  delay  statement  has been enclosed. The 
Committee expects the Ministry to be cautious in such matters and ensure compliance 
with the time schedule for laying of notifications in future.  
             
VI  Ministry of Urban Development & Poverty Alleviation 
  
      The Committee regrets to note that out of two notifications laid during the 196 th 
Session, one has been delayed by four months.   The Committee expects the Ministry to 
take necessary corrective action in order to ensure that such delays do not recur and the 
schedule as prescribed by the Committee in the matter of laying of Subordinate 
Legislation is followed strictly. 
  

3.   The Committee also notes with regret the delayed laying of notification at s l. No. 10 
of the Annexure by the Ministry of Civil Aviation by four months and that too without 
any delay statement.   
  
4.   The Committee impresses upon all the Ministries/Departments to take immediate 
steps to avoid delay in laying of subordinate legisl ation. The Committee, accordingly, 
wishes to bring to the notice of all Ministries/Departments of Government of India, 
particularly, the defaulting ones as enumerated above the following recommendations as 
contained in its 131 st Report wherein a time sched ule for the laying of subordinate 
legislation has been prescribed as follows: 
  
“Orders required to be laid before the House should be laid  (i) if the House is not 
in Session, during the Session immediately following the date of publication of the 
Order in the Official Gazette and (ii) if the House is in Session, on the date of the 
publication of the Order, during its continuance and in case the time lag between 
the date of publication and the date of the closing of the Session is less than 15 
clear days, before the expiry of   the  Session immediately following the said 
Session.   
All the Ministries/Departments of Government of India should henceforth comply 
with this schedule in the matter of laying of the orders issued under various Acts 
of Parliament on the Table of the Rajya Sabha.” 
  
 5.  The Committee also reiterates its following observations made in its 135 th Report 
regarding appending of delay statement where there has been delay in the laying: 
  
“ The Committee has, time and again, emphasized that it is essential that in case 
there is a delay in the laying of Statutory Orders, the concerned 
Ministry/Department should invariably append a delay statement along with the 
notifications being laid so as to apprise the Parliament of the causes of delay.  The 
Committee desires all Ministries/Departments to take a note of this, since the 
intention is that through the process of formulation of a delay st atement the 
Ministry is able to introspect, identifying bottlenecks and devising remedial 
measures”.

      The Committee met at 3.30 p.m. on Monday,   the 9th December, 2002 in Room No.  
126-C (Chairman’s Room) Third Floor, Parliament House, New Delhi. 
                         
MEMBERS PRESENT 
  
      1.   Shri A. Vijayaraghavan    Chairman                       
            2.   Dr. A.R. Kidwai 
            3.   Shri B.P. Singhal

SECRETARIAT 
  
      1.   Shri N.C. Joshi, Joint Secretary

4.   Shri Arun Sharma, Committee Officer 
  
2.       The Committee took up for consideration its draft 145 th Report on the Statutory 
Orders laid on the table of the Rajya Sabha during the 196 th Session.  While considering 
the Report, the Committee also had a look into the delay in the laying of Statutory Orders 
by the various Ministries/Departments during the previous five to six Sessions and it 
noted that the delay in laying had been quite persistent.   The Committee further noted 
that in majority of such cases of delay, the Ministries/ Departments had even failed to 
append a delay statement explaining the reasons for delay in the laying of 
the  notifications despite Committees’ specific  and  clear recommendations to that effect  
in its 131 st Report which had been reiterated a number of times.  The Committee, 
accordingly, decided to hear the representatives   of the Ministries of Finance and 
Company Affairs and Home Affairs on the question of persistent delay in the laying of 
their notifications. 
  
3.   The Committee, thereafter, adopted its draft 145th Report and decided to present 
it to the House on the 12th December, 2002.  The Committee authorized the Chairman 
and in his absence Shri B.P.Singhal and Shri Ravula Chandra Sekar Reddy MPs to 
present the Report. 
  
4.   The Committee also decided to meet again at 3.00 p.m. on the 9th January, 2003. 
  
5.  The meeting then adjourned at 4.30  p.m.

            I, the Chairman of the Committee on Subordinate Legislation, having been 
authorized by the Committee to present the Report on its behalf, do hereby present this

. 
The Committee considered and adopted the Report in its meeting held on  31.03.2003. 
  
1.3       The notifications containing Rules/Regulations, etc. laid on the Table of the 
Rajya Sabha during its 197th session have been perused by the Committee in the light of 
the provisions of the Acts under which these were framed and also with a view to seeing 
whether these have been laid within the prescribed time-frame and properly.  The 
Committee’s observations/recommendations are contained in the report that follows.  
   
  

new delhi 
March 31,2003 
A. VIJAYARAGHAVAN  
Chairman 
 Committee on Subordinate Legislation, 
 Rajya Sabha 
  
 
Report 
  
I 
Laying of Statutory Orders on the Table of  Rajya Sabha 
  
            During the 197th Session of the Rajya Sabha, 233 Statutory Orders were laid on 
the Table of the House by various Ministries/Departments.  The details of the Gazette 
Notifications in which these were published and the date of their laying on the Table of 
the Rajya Sabha have been indicated in the Ministry-wise statement placed at 
Annexure. 
  
2.         During the course of scrutiny of these Orders, the Committee has noted some 
cases where there has been a considerable time lag between the date of notification of 
the Order and the date of its laying. The annexed statement also indicates the period of 
delay in cases where notifications have not been laid as per the Committee’s guidelines 
and whether such notifications were accompanied by a statement indicating the reasons 
for delay in laying.  In some of the cases the delay has been quite abnormal.  The 
observations/ recommendations of the Committee in respect of specific 
Ministries/Departments are as follows: - 
I           Ministry of Commerce & Industry: 
            The Committee regrets to note that the Ministry of Commerce and Industry 
have delayed the laying of 3 of their notifications (sl. nos. 6 to 8 of the Annexure) out of 
the 8 notifications laid by them during the Session. Appropriately, notification at sl. no. 
8 could have been laid during the Budget (195th) Session of 2002 and the notifications at 
sl. nos. 6 and 7 during the Monsoon (196th) Session. The Ministry have also failed to 
append the delay statement along with these 3 notifications as has been recommended 
by the Committee. There had been cases of delay in laying by this Ministry during the 
196th and 197th Sessions also in pursuance to which the Committee had recommended 
the Ministry to take suitable remedial action. The Committee hopes that the Ministry of 
Commerce & Industry would take prompt remedial action and comply with the 
prescribed schedule in the matter of laying of subordinate legislation. 

  
II         Ministry of  Communication & Information Technology: 
             
The Committee regrets to note that out of the 5 notifications laid by this Ministry, there 
has been an inordinate delay of one year and nine months in case of notification at sl. 
no. 15 and 6 months in case of notification at sl. no. 17. The Ministry have even failed to 
append the delay statement in the former case where the delay has been very large. The 
Committee has come across some instances of delay in case of this Ministry in the past 
sessions also like in the 191st, 194th and 196th Sessions of the Rajya Sabha. The 
Committee would like the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology to 
take necessary corrective measures so as to ensure the compliance of the Committee’s 
recommendations in the matter of laying of subordinate legislation. 
  
III        Ministry of Environment & Forests: 
  
The Committee is unhappy to note that the Ministry of Environment & Forests did not 
comply with the schedule for laying in case of 10 out of 12 notifications laid during the 
197th Session and the delay ranging from 1 year to 4 years 4 months as shown in the 
Annexure (sl. nos. 24 to 33).  The Committee suggests that the Ministry of Environment 
& Forests should take immediate corrective action and ensure that henceforth the 
Subordinate Legislation is laid before the Parliament on time. 
  
IV        Ministry of Finance & Company Affairs: 
  
            The Committee is extremely unhappy to note that the Ministry of Finance and 
Company Affairs have not complied with the schedule for laying of the notifications as 
prescribed by the Committee in its 131st Report for the eighth consecutive session of the 
Rajya Sabha. The Ministry have laid 129 rules/regulations during the 197th Session and 
there has been delay in case of 77 ranging from 4 months to 12 months as shown in the 
Annexure and delay statement has been appended only in 8 cases.  
            The Committee, being concerned over the persistent delay in the laying of 
Subordinate Legislation by the Ministry of Finance eversince it had started examining 
this aspect from the 191st Session onwards on a regular basis, heard the Secretary, 
Ministry of Finance along with the Secretaries of different Departments under the 
Ministry on the question of non-compliance of the schedule as laid down by the 
Committee in this behalf on the 9th January 2003. During the course of the oral 
evidence, the Finance Secretary, while admitting delay in laying, assured the Committee 
that they were taking appropriate remedial action in order to avoid such delays for 
future. The Committee hopes that there would be concerted efforts on the part of 

Ministry would help to eliminate such instances of delay in laying of Subordinate 
Legislation in future.  
  
V         Ministry of Health & Family Welfare: 
  
            The Committee is unhappy to note that out of the 5 notifications laid (sl. nos. 
164-168), there has been a delay of 4 months in laying of two notifications and no delay 
statement has been annexed therewith.  There were instances of delay in a number of 
cases during the 192nd and 194th to 196th Sessions also. The Committee hopes that the 
Ministry of Health & Family Welfare would take adequate steps to ensure compliance 
with the time schedule as laid down by the Committee for the laying of Subordinate 
Legislation in future. 
  
VI        Ministry of Home Affairs: 
  
            The Committee notes with regret that there has been a delay of 4 months and 7 
months in case of laying two notifications (sl. nos. 171 and 174) out of 6 notifications 
laid.  The delay statement was enclosed only in one case (Sl No. 174). There were 
instances of delay in a number of cases during the 192nd and 194th to 196th Sessions also. 
Keeping in view the fact that there had been delay in laying in a fairly large number of 
cases from the 191st Session onwards of the Rajya Sabha eversince the Committee have 
taken up such a scrutiny on a regular basis, the Committee heard the oral evidence of 
the Secretary, Home Affairs on the 9th January 2003. During the course of the oral 
evidence, the Committee was assured that the Ministry were taking suitable action to 
avoid recurrence of such delays in future. The Committee hopes that the Ministry of 
Home Affairs would be able to keep to their promise.  
  
VII          Ministry of Human Resource Development: 
  
            The Committee notes with regret that there is a delay in laying in all the three 
notifications laid by the Ministry of Human Resource Development during the 197th 
Session (sl nos. 175 to 177). There had been instances of delay in laying in a number of 
cases during the 191st and 194th to 196th Sessions also. The Committee would like the 
Ministry to streamline their procedures so as to obviate such instances in future. 
  
VIII     Ministry of Information & Broadcasting :  

  
            The Committee is distressed to note that out of the 12 notifications laid during 
the 197th Session, 10 have been delayed by period ranging from 6 to 7 months.  Further, 
delay statement has been enclosed only with four notifications  (sl. nos. 181, 183, 187 & 
188).  The Committee expects that the Ministry of Information & Broadcasting would 
take appropriate steps to comply with time schedule laid by the Committee for the 
laying of Subordinate Legislation. 
  
IX        Ministry of Labour: 
  
            The Committee regrets to note that out of the 5 notifications laid by the Ministry, 
there has been delay in 2 cases (sl. nos. 193 & 194) by 5 and 6 months, respectively, and 
no delay statement has been appended. There were instances of delay in a considerable 
number of cases during the 191st, 192nd, 194th and 196th sessions also.  The Committee 
recommends the Ministry to stick to the time schedule as recommended by the 
Committee in its 135th Report in laying the   Subordinate Legislation before the 
Parliament. 
  
X         Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions:  
  
             The Committee notes with regret that the Ministry of Personnel,  Public 
Grievances and Pensions have  laid 16 rules/regulations  during the 197th Session out of 
which 12 have been delayed by period ranging from 7 months to 19 months. There were 
instances of delay during the 191st to 193rd Sessions also. The Committee expects the 
Ministry to be cautious in such matters and ensure compliance with time schedule for 
laying the notifications in future. 
  
XI        Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas: 
  
            The Committee notes that two notifications laid by the Ministry of Petroleum  & 
Natural   Gas have been delayed by 9 to 10 months (sl. nos. 213 & 214).  The Ministry 
have also not enclosed the delay statement giving the reasons for the delay in 
laying.  The Committee expects the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas to exercise 
caution in such matters and ensure that the schedule as prescribed by the Committee in 
the matter of laying of Subordinate Legislation framed under various Acts of 
Parliament is followed meticulously in future. 
  

XII  Ministry of Power: 
  
            The Committee regrets to note the Ministry of Power have laid 3 notifications 
during the 197th Session out of which 2 have been delayed by 4 to 5 months (sl. nos. 215 
and 216).  The Committee expects the Ministry to be cautious in such matters and 
ensure compliance with time schedule for laying the rules/regulations in future. 
  
XIII  Ministry of Shipping:   
  
            The Committee notes that there has been an extreme delay of 2 years and 7 
months on the part of the Ministry in laying 2 of its notifications (sl nos. 230 & 
231).  There were instances of delay in a  
  
number of cases during the 194th and 196th Sessions also. The Committee would like the 
Ministry of Shipping to take remedial measure to prevent recurrence of such action and 
also ensure that henceforth the Subordinate Legislation is laid before the Parliament on 
time. 
  
3.   The Committee impresses upon all the Ministries/Departments to take immediate 
steps to avoid delay in laying of subordinate legislation. The Committee, accordingly, 
wishes to bring to the notice of all Ministries/Departments of Government of India, 
particularly, the defaulting ones as enumerated above the following recommendations 
as contained in its 131st Report wherein a time schedule for the laying of subordinate 
legislation has been prescribed as follows: 
“Orders required to be laid before the House should be laid  (i) if the House is not in 
Session, during the Session immediately following the date of publication of the Order 
in the Official Gazette and (ii) if the House is in Session, on the date of the publication of 
the Order, during its continuance and in case the time lag between the date of 
publication and the date of the closing of the Session is less than 15 clear days, before 
the expiry of  the  Session immediately following the said Session. All the 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India should henceforth comply with this 
schedule in the matter of laying of the orders issued under various Acts of Parliament 
on the Table of the Rajya Sabha.” 
  
 4.        The Committee also reiterates its following observations made in its 135th Report 
regarding appending of delay statement where there has been delay in the laying: 

 “ The Committee has, time and again, emphasized that it is essential that in case there 
is a delay in the laying of Statutory Orders, the concerned Ministry/Department should 
invariably append a delay statement along with the notifications being laid so as to 
apprise the Parliament of the causes of delay.  The Committee desires all 
Ministries/Departments to take a note of this,   since   the intention is that through the 
process of formulation of a delay statement the Ministry is able to introspect, identifying 
bottlenecks and devising remedial measures”.

I
VISAKHAPATNAM Port EMPLOYEES (GRANT OF ADVANCES FOR
- PURCHASE OF CONVEYANCES) REGULATIONS, 1993

The Visakhapatnam Port Employees (Grant of Advances for

Purchase of Conveyance), Regulations, 1993 framed under the Major
~ Port Trusts Act, 1963 were examined and a questionnaire was

forwarded to the Ministry of Shipping on October 31, 2001. The
Ministry furnished their replies on the various points raised in the
Questionnaire and the matter was discussed with the representatives of
the Visakhapatnam Port Trust as well as the Ministry of Shipping at
Visakhapatnam-on the 9" November 2001. The points raised in the
Questionnaire, the Ministry's comments thereon together with the
observation of the Committee are as follows.:-
1. Point raised

Whether. the Visakhapatnam Port Employees (Grant of
» Advances for purchase of Conveyance) Regulations, 1993 and the
amendments thereto have been laid on the Table of both the Houses of
Parliament, if so; the details in this regard?.

Ministry’s reply ‘

The Visakhapatnam Port Employees (Grant of Advances for
Purchase of Conveyance) Regulations, 1993 were laid on the Table of
Lok Sabha on 2.8.94 and Rajya Sabha on 27.7.94. The subsequent
amendment vide GSR No. 280(E) dated 27.5.97 was also laid on the
Table of Lok Sabha on 8.5.2000 and Rajya Sabha on 2.5.2000.

1

/



2
Committee’s Observation
There had been a in laying the amendment regulations notified
on 27.5.1997 due to oversight. The Committee observed that such a
delay in laying should be avoided.

2. . Point raised

The Regulations under examination have been framed in the
year 1993 under the Major Port Trusts Act, 1963. What are the reasons
for delay in the enactment of the regulations and in what manner grant
of advance for purchase of conveyance was regulated in the absence of
these regulations?

Ministry’s reply

It is to submit that prior to enactment of the Major Port Trusts
Act, 1963, which came into force from the 29" February, 1964, the
Rules of the Central Government were made applicable to the
employees of the Port. After the enactment of the MPT Act, 1963, the
Central Government framed certain Regulations as first Regulations
under Section 126 of the MPT Act. However, in respect of grant of
.advances for purchase of motor cycle/motor car, no such first
Regulations have been framed and as such, the Port Trust adopted the
Government Rules viz., GFRs and the provisions relating to the grant of
advances for motor cycle/motor car, etc. as available in GFRs were
followed by the Port Trust. For the first time in the year 1989, a
Proposal framing Regulations entitled VPE (Grant of Advances for
purchase of conveyances) Regulations, 1989 was placed before the
VPT Board, vide Agenda item No. 43 in the meeting held on the 23"



3
January, 1989 and Board’s approval sent to Government for sanction,
wherein it was clearly mentioned that the VPT had no separate
Regulations for grant of advances for purchase of conveyances by the
port employees and hence the provisions in GFRs were followed.
Thereafter, certain clarifications were sought by the Ministry and again
the said Regulations were placed before the Board, vide Agenda item
No. 31 in the meeting held on 29" January, 1992 and again, on further
directions from the Ministry to redraft the Regulations in conformity
with the provisions of either the Rules prevailing in other Port Trusts or
adopting the provisions contained in GFRs, as applicable to the Central
Government servants, the Regulations were revised and were placed
before the Board, vide Agenda item No. 5-5 in its meeting held on 29"
March, 1993 and the said Regulations were approved, vide Resolution
No. 278/92-93 and sent to the Government vide letter dated the 28”
April, 1993, seeking approval of the Government. Finally, the
Regulations have been approved by the Government vide Notification
No. 1/PR/12015/14/91-PE-I dated 3" January, 1994 and published in
the Gazette of India as GSR No. 1-8 dated 3" January, 1994.

. Hence, immediately after formation of VPT Board, the
provisions of GFRs of the Central Government have been followed
and after framing the Regulations as mentioned above, the same are
being followed and the Government instructions/orders are also being
followed, vide Regulation 26 of the said Regulations.



Committee’s Observation

The Committee noted the Ministry’s reply regarding the
manner in which the grant of conveyance advance was being regulated
when the regulations were not in place.
3. Point raised

What is the justification for excluding persons appointed on
deputation from the Central or a State Government for the purpose of

rant of advance for purchase of conveyances? Whether it would be

possible to include such employees.also for the purpose. What are the
comments? ;

हे

Ministry’s reply

It is to submit that the reason for excluding the persons on
deputation from Central or State Government or any other source is that
the period of deputation is for a limited period and on completion of
deputation period, they will be repatriated to the parent department and
if advances are granted during the period of deputation, difficulty may
be experienced in recovering the said advance from the employee(s)
who are/were repatriated to various organizations.

हु Committee’s Observation

The Committee noted the Ministry’s reply.
4. Point raised

As per regulation 6(2), an employee holding class I post
whose basic pay is in the scale the maximum of which is Rs. 7500/- per
month or more, is entitled for advance of purchase of motor car. These
provisions of the regulations give an impression as if the scales of pay


5
have not been revised for long in pursuance of the recommendations of
the Central Pay Commission made from time to time. What is the
present status in this regard?

Ministry’s reply
It is to submit that initially the maximum scale of pay of
Class-I Post has been mentioned as Rs. 4230/- in the Regulations
approved by the Government and published in the Gazette and
thereafter the said scale of pay has been amended to Rs. 7,500/- vide
“GSR No. 280(E) dated 27" May,1997. Now, the said maximum scale
of pay of the said Class-I posts has been revised to Rs. 15,100/-, while
revising pay scales of Class- I & II officers, which came into force on
1.1.97 and in terms of the said revised scales of pay, the maximum
scale of pay of Class-I post has been taken into consideration for the
purpose of granting motor car advance, pending amendment to
Regulations, which is presently under consideration.
Committee’s Observation
The Committee noted the reply and desired that the Ministry
should amend the pay scales mentioned in the regulations since the
same had been revised.
5. Point raised Regulation 12
The last revision in the advances for purchase of conveyances
took place in the year 1997. However, the repayment schedules was
not revised. There appears to be a need for revision of the repayment
schedules keeping in view the cost of vehicles and advance. Whether

Ce a ee



6
any review has taken place in this regard. Whether the Ministry intend
to revise the repayment schedules?

Ministry’s reply

It is to submit that Regulation 12 of the said Regulations deals
with recovery of advance and the number of instalments for recovery
shall be not more than 150 instalments in respect of motor car and 100
instalments in respect of motor cycle. However, in Rule No. 201 of
GFRs (Swamy’s compilation 2000), a provision exists that the
maximum number of instalments where the motor car advance is
Tequired to be recovered was mentioned as 200. In respect of motor
cycles, a provision exists in Rule 211 second proviso indicating the
maximum number of instalments as 70 (Swamy’s compilation of GFR,
2000 edition). The recovery of advance will depend upon the length
of left over service of the concerned officer, who had been granted
motor car advance. Hence, it is felt that it is not necessary to modify
the number of instalments for recovery of advances as mentioned in the
Regulation.

Committee’s Observation

. The Committee desired that the Ministry should consider

revising the number of instalments for repaying of car loan from 150 to
200. —

6. Point raised
Regulation’ 19 mentioned in the sub-regulation (4) of

regulation 6 appears to be a printing mistake. Should it not be
regulation 18, whether the Ministry would correct it?



Ministry’s reply

It is to submit that Regulation 6 deals with condition of
eligibility and sub-regulation (4) deals with granting of advance for the
second time, unless the outstanding balance of the first advance is
repaid in full with interest. In this sub-regulation, a reference to
Regulation-19 has been mentioned as an exception. The present issue
for consideration is whether the said Regulation is 18 or 19. In this
connection, it is to submit that Regulation-18 deals with condition for
grant of a second or subsequent advance before the earlier advance with
interest has been repaid. Regulation-19 deals with restrictions in the

REPORT 
I 
Laying of Statutory Orders on the Table of Rajya Sabha 

      During the 198th Session of the Rajya Sabha, 592 Statutory Orders were laid on the 
Table of the House by various Ministries/Departments. The details of the Gazette 
Notifications in which these were publ ished and the date of their laying on the Table of 
the Rajya Sabha have been indicated in the Ministry-wise statement placed at Annexure. 
2.   During the course of scrutiny of these Orders, the Committee has noted some cases 
where there has been a considerable time lag between the date of notification of the Order 
and the date of its laying. The annexed statement also indicates the period of delay in 
cases where notifications have not been laid as per the Committee's guidelines and 
whether such notification s were accompanied by a statement indicating the reasons for 
the delay in laying. In some of the cases the delay has been quite abnormal. The 
observations/ recommendations of the Committee in respect of the specific 
Ministries/Departments are as follows :– 
I.    Ministry of Coal 
      The Committee notes that the Ministry of Coal have delayed the laying of 1 of their 
notifications (Sl. No. 14) out of the 4 notifications laid by them during the Session. The 
Ministry have also not appended any delay statement  with the notification. The 
Committee hopes that the Ministry of Coal shall adhere to the time schedule as 
recommended by the Committee in laying the Subordinate Legislation pertaining to 
them. 
II.   Ministry of Commerce & Industry 
      The Committee regr ets to note that the Ministry of Commerce & Industry have 
delayed the laying of 6 of their notifications (Sl. No. 18 & 31 to 35) out of the 22 
notifications laid by them during the 198th session. Notification at Sl. No. 18 was not even 
accompanied by a delay statement. Appropriately, notifications at Sl. Nos. 31 to 35 could 
have been laid during Monsoon (196th) Session or thereafter during Winter (197th) 
Session of 2002. The Ministry have practically laid these notifications after about one year 
of their publication. The delay statement of the Ministry is also not convincing as it simply 
states that sufficient time was not available during the Winter Session which had resulted 
in delay. The Committee is extremely unhappy to note that the Ministry of Commerce & 
Industry did not comply with the time schedule laid by the Committee for laying of 
Subordinate Legislation. The Committee recommends the Ministry of Commerce and 
Industry should stick to the time schedule as recommended by the Committee in its 131st 
Report in laying the Subordinate Legislation before the Parliament. 
III.Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution 
      The Committee is unhappy to note that the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & 
Public Distribution have delayed the laying of 2 of their notifications (Sl. Nos. 49 & 50) 
out of the 7 notifications laid by them during the Session. The notification at Sl. No. 50 
could have been laid during theWinter (197th) Session and the notification  at Sl. No. 49 
even before i.e., during the Monsoon (196th) Session, 2002. Further, the delayed 
notifications were not accompanied by delay statements. The Committee would like to 
draw attention of the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution towards 
the schedule prescribed by it in the matter of laying of Subordinate Legislation and it 
hopes that this would be complied with in future. 
IV.Ministry of Environment and Forests 
      The Committee notes that the Ministry of Environment and Forests have delayed the 
laying of 2 of their notifications (Sl. Nos. 54 & 55) out of the 5 notifications laid by them 
during the session. There had been a delay of approximately 4 & 5 months in laying the 

notifications and no delay statements had been appended  to the notifications. The 
Committee hopes that the Ministry of Environment and Forests would observe the time 
schedule prescribed by it for laying of Subordinate Legislation in future. 
V.  Ministry of Finance 
      The Committee is extremely unhappy to note that the Ministry of Finance have again 
not complied with the schedule for laying of the notifications as prescribed by the 
Committee. The Ministry have laid 349 rules/regulations during the 198th session and 
there has been delay in case of 38 notificat ions ranging from 3 months to 10 months. 
Besides, there are 7 cases of delay exceeding one year (Sl. Nos. 104, 296 to 301) and one 
case of delay exceeding two years (Sl. No. 193). Further there has been one case of 
exceptional delay in laying (Sl. No. 264) where there has been a delay of 6 years. The delay 
statements have been appended only in 11 cases. In case of the notification at Sl. No. 264 
where there is a delay of over 6 years, the Ministry in their delay statement have simply 
stated that the reasons for delay were "not willful". This is not an acceptable explanation 
for delay. In another case (Sl. No. 273) the statement of delay as appended by the Ministry 
states – "Notification No. 16/2002 Service Tax dated 2.8.2002 could not be laid on the 
Table of  Rajya Sabha in the last session because of certain unforeseen circumstances 
beyond the control of the section."  The reason of delay given by the Ministry is not 
convincing. In other two cases (Sl. Nos. 322 & 323), the statement of delay appended by 
the Ministry states – "the notifications were sent on 12.12.2002 for laying before the Rajya 
Sabha for 17.12.2002 and Lok Sabha for 20.12.2002. The Rajya Sabha Secretariat refused 
to accept the same for laying due to shortage of time, and the house adjourned on 
21.12.2002. Hence the delay". In this context, it is stated that the last date of receiving 
notifications for laying on 17.12.2002 was 11.12.2002 and the notifications were brought 
to the Rajya Sabha Secretariat on 12.12.2002 i.e. after the due date. Further, the date of 
publication of both these notifications were 14.8.2002 and 30.9.2002 respectively, and 
evidently these could have been laid during the Winter (197th) Session or the first half of 
the Budget Session. Hence, the reasons of delay attributed by the Ministry of Finance are 
not justified. It may be recalled that the Committee had heard the Secretary, Ministry of 
Finance on the question of non -compliance of the time schedule in the matter of timely 
laying of Subordinate Legislation on the 9th Janua ry, 2003. During the course of oral 
evidence, the Finance Secretary, while admitting delay in laying, had assured the 
Committee that they shall take appropriate remedial action to avoid delay in future. The 
Committee expects the Ministry to be cautious in such matters and would take concerted 
steps to eliminate such instances of delay in laying of Subordinate Legislation in future. 
VI.Ministry of Home Affairs 
      The Committee notes that the Ministry of Home Affairs have delayed the laying of 
one of their notification (Sl. No. 404) by 6 months and no delay statement was annexed. 
The notification could have been laid during the preceding (197th) session. The 
Committee expects the Ministry to be cautious in such matters and ensure compliance 
with time schedule for laying the notifications in future. 
VII.   Ministry of Human Resource Development 
      The Committee notes with regret that there is delay in laying of 2 out of the 3 
notifications laid by the Ministry of Human Resource Development during the 198th  
Session (Sl. Nos. 407 & 408). The notifications having been published on the 18th 
November, 2002, the Ministry could have laid them during the 197th (Winter) Session, 
2002 itself. The Ministry also failed to append the requisite delay statement with both 
these notifications. There had been instances of delay in laying in some cases during the 

194th, 195th & 197th Sessions also. The Committee would like the Ministry to take 
necessary corrective measures so as to avoid such instances of delay in future. 
VIII.Ministry of Information & Broadcasting 
      The Committee notes with regret that the only notification (Sl. No. 410) laid by the 
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting has been delayed by 4 months and no delay 
statement has been enclosed therewith. The C ommittee hopes that the Ministry of 
Information & Broadcasting shall adhere to the time schedule as recommended by it for 
laying the Subordinate Legislation before the Parliament. 
IX.Ministry of Labour 
      The Committee notes with regret that there is a delay of over two years in laying of 1 
out of 4 notifications laid by Ministry of Labour (Sl. No. 411). The Committee takes note 
of the explanation for delay as given by the Ministry in the delay statement and hopes 
that such instances of delay shall not occur in future. 
X.  Ministry of Power 
      The Committee notes with regret that there is delay in laying of 1 out of the 2 
notifications laid by the Ministry of Power by 5 months and the Ministry have not 
appended any delay statement. The Committee hopes that the Ministry would ensure 
strict compliance of the schedule for laying Subordinate Legislation as prescribed by the 
Committee in its 131st report. 
XI.Ministry of Railways 
      The Committee notes with regret that the Ministry of Railways have laid 7 
rules/regulations during the 198th session out of which 5 have been delayed by period 
ranging from 5 months to one year. There were instances of delayed laying during the 
197th session also. Further, the Ministry have appended delay statement only in one case 
(Sl. No. 424). The Committee expects the Ministry to be cautious in such matters and 
ensure compliance with time schedule for laying the notifications in future. 
XII.   Ministry of Road Transport & Highways 
      The Committee notes that the Ministry o f Road Transport and Highways have 
delayed in laying of 12 notifications out of the total of 143 notifications laid. The delay in 
laying range from 4-5 months and the Ministry have also appended reasons for delay in 
laying with these notifications during t he 198th session. The Committee expects the 
Ministry to be more prompt and vigilant in laying the rules/regulations within the 
stipulated period to obviate such instances of delay in future. 
XIII.Ministry of Shipping 
      The Committee notes with regret that the Ministry of Shipping delayed the laying of 
2 of their notifications (Sl. Nos. 570 & 577) by 5 to 6 months. The Ministry also did not 
enclose the delay statements giving reasons for delay in laying. The Committee expects 
the Ministry of Shipping to exercise caution in such matters and ensure the laying of 
Subordinate Legislation within the time schedule. 
3.   The Committee impresses upon all the Ministries/Departments to take immediate 
steps to avoid delay in laying of Subordinate Legislation. The Co mmittee, accordingly, 
wishes to bring to the notice of all Ministries/Departments of the Government of India, 
particularly, the defaulting ones as enumerated above the following recommendations, as 
contained in its 131st Report wherein a time schedule for the laying of Subordinate 
legislation has been prescribed, as follows : 

      "Orders required to be laid before the House should be laid (i) if the House is not in 
Session, during the Session immediately following the date of publication of the 
Order in t he Official Gazette and (ii) if the House is in Session, on the date of the 
publication of the Order, during its continuance and in case the time lag between the 
date of publication and the date of closing of the Session is less than 15 clear days, 
before the expiry of the Session immediately following the said Session. All the 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India should henceforth comply with this 
schedule in the matter of laying of the orders issued under various Acts of Parliament 
on the Table of the Rajya Sabha." 
4.   The Committee also reiterates its following observations made in its 135th Report 
regarding appending of delay statement where there has been delay in the laying : 
          "The Committee has, time and again, emphasized that it is  essential that in case 
there is a delay in the laying of Statutory Orders, the concerned Ministry/Department 
should invariably append a delay statement along with the notifications being laid so as 
to apprise Parliament of the causes of delay. The Committ ee desires all 
Ministries/Departments to take a note of this, since the intension is that through the 
process of formulation of a delay statement the Ministry is able to introspect, identifying 
bottlenecks and devise remedial measures".

REPORT 
I 
THE  PRESS  COUNCIL  ACT,  1978 ---- IMPLEMENTATION  OF  109TH 
REPORT  OF  THE  COMMITTEE  ON  SUBORDINATE  LEGISLATION, 
RAJYA  SABHA 
      The Committee examined framing of the subordinate legistation under the Press 
Council Act, 1978 and in its 57th Report, presented to the House on the 22nd December, 
1983. recommended as under: 
"20.      The Committee recommends that in case where multiple agencies are 
involved in the matter of finalisation of rules, the practice should be to call the 
representatives of all the concerned Ministries, Departments, etc. simultaneously, 
round the table, for discussion instead of writing to one authority or the other. Such 

a meeting may be repeated if necessary for speedy decisions and expeditious 
finalisation of the rules and regulatons. 
21.The Committee finds it difficult to agree with the Gove rnment's plea that in the 
absence of regulations duly framed by the Press Council, and approved by 
Government, there was no vacuum in so far as conditions of services of the Council's 
employees were concerned and that until the regulations are so made and notified 
the conditions of service governing the Central Government employees were being 
applied to the Council's employees. The Committee feels that the Press Council has 
a specific and autonomous role to perform and conditions of service of its employees 
have to be drawn up independently in consonance with the nature of its functions. 
The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that the rules and regulations for 
the Press Council's employees be finalised with utmost expeditiousness, eliminating 
all delay."  
2.   The Committee, in its 109th Report, presented to the House on the 29th May, 1995, 
took an adverse note of the very slow pace of the action being taken on its above 
recommendations by the Ministry of Information & Broadcasting. The Committee 
reiterated its earlier recommendations stating that the Ministry should frame the 
regulations relating to service conditions of the employees of the Press Council of India 
(PCI) under Section 26 of the Press Council Act, 1978 expeditiously. 
3.   In response, the Ministry in their communication dated the 2nd August, 1995 accepted 
the Committee's recommendations and stated that efforts were being made to implement 
the same. The Ministry sought extension of time up to the 31 st July, 1996 vide their 
subsequent communication dated the 8 th July 1996. Being not able to get a satisfactory 
reply from the Ministry despite exchange of a number of communications, the Chairman 
of the Committee, on the 22nd June, 2000, addressed a letter to the then Minister of State 
for Infor mation & Broadcasting drawing his attention to the Committee's 
recommendations on the subject in the past and requesting for expediting action thereon. 
In response thereto, the Hon'ble Minister vide, communication dated the 6th September, 
2000, responded as follows : 
       "I would like to assure you that this Ministry has been making continuous efforts 
to finalize the regulations in consultation with the Press Council of India. The 
provisions of Section 26 of the Press Council Act enjoin upon the Press Co uncil of 
India to frame regulations, specifying the terms and conditions of service of its 
employees, with the approval of the Ministry. Time and again, the proposals have 
been examined and forwarded to the Press Council of India for notification but no 
finality could be reached. Despite several inter -ministerial meetings, the areas of 
difference have narrowed down but have not been eliminated. It will be appreciated 
that if the regulations have to be framed in consultation with the Ministry of 
Information and Broadcasting and the Ministry of Finance, then they will have to 
conform to the pattern that exists for employees of other autonomous bodies. 
       I would like to suggest that the Committee should direct the Council, which is 
directly responsible for taking action in terms of the statute, to notify the regulations 
as approved by the Ministry. Minor differences, if any that remain, can be discussed 
separately and suitably incorporated later on." 
4.   Thereafter, in pursuance to a communication, a backg round note was received from 
the Press Council of India on the subject on the 3rd November, 2000 (Annexure I) wherein 
it was explained that the Council prepared the draft regulations for regulating the terms 
and conditions of service of its employees and forwarded the same to the Ministry as early 
as in 1982 but no clearance could be received due to absence of consensus on some of its 

provisions. The Council, in between, revised the regulations in 1997 and again in early 
2000 and forwarded the same to the M inistry for clearance but there was no positive 
response from the Ministry. 
 5.  Keeping in view the status of the matter, the Committee heard the representatives of 
the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting as well as the Press Council of India on the 
8th January, 2001. During the course of the oral evidence, the Secretary, Ministry of 
Information and Broadcasting, explained to the Committee the points on which there was 
a difference of opinion with the Press Council of India resulting in delay in finalization of 
the rules. According to the Ministry of Finance, autonomous bodies funded by the 
Government could not be allowed to create posts and fix pay scales of their own, without 
the concurrence of the Government. Another point on which there was a diffe rence of 
opinion was that the Press Council wanted their employees to be given the benefit of 
pension but, in the opinion of the Ministry of Finance, this could not be done through 
regulations without Government's concurrence. On the contrary, Secretary, t he Press 
Council of India, while pleading the cause of autonomy for the Council, pointed out that 
the Council had already more or less conceded to all the objections of the Ministry with 
regard to the provisions of the draft regulations and it was not poss ible for them to 
concede to a total abrogation of its powers which have been conferred upon the Council 
by the Parliament. The Council, being a quasi -judicial body, could not be reduced to an 
appendage of the Government of India or treated as a subordinate /attached office of the 
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting. In support of this contention of the Press 
Council of India, the Committee's attention was also invited towards the provisions of 
Rule 8 and 8A of the Press Council of India Rules. Rule 8 stip ulated that the employees 
of the Council would enjoy the same terms and conditions of service and rights and 
privileges as the employees of the Central Government. Later on, Rule 8A had been 
inserted in the rules which provided that all proposals relating to emoluments, structure 
including adoption of pay scales, allowances and revision of scales and creation of the 
posts, where maximum of the pay scales exceeded Rs. 15,200/ - per month, shall be made 
only with the prior approval of the Central Government. T he contention of the 
representatives of the Press Council of India before the Committee was that the 
conditions being spelt out by the Ministry of Finance were a direct negation of the 
provision of Rule 8A. 
6.   The Committee, after hearing the view point of the Government as well as the Press 
Council of India, directed the Secretary, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting to 
send a note giving the extent to which Government were agreeable for allowing financial 
autonomy to the Press Council of India. The  Secretary, Ministry of Information and 
Broadcasting, agreed to furnish the note by the first week of Ferbruary, 2001. 
7.   In the absence of any substantial response from the Ministry of Information and 
Broadcasting, the Committee again heard the represen tatives of Information and 
Broadcasting as well as the Press Council of India on the 28 th January, 2002. The 
Committee, at the outset, took a strong exception on the failure to furnish the promised 
note on the financial autonomy even after the lapse of almost one year. During the course 
of oral evidence, the Committee was apprised of the efforts made by the Ministry of 
Information and Broadcating for arriving at a consensus on the pending issues of the 
Press Council of India. It was stated that the Ministry were trying their level best to sort 
out the issues and, in fact, the difference of opinion had really narrowed down on the 
question of freedom to be given to the Press Council of India to create posts. In this 
context, the Ministry of Finance had gone al ong with the Ministry of Information and 
Broadcasting to a very large extent by agreeing that if the Press Council of India effected 
matching savings in respect of the salaries, they could create posts meaning thereby that 

the Press Council of India could create some posts by abolishing some other posts so that 
there were matching savings. But, the Press Council of India wanted some more flexibility 
in this regard by allowing them to show matching savings under the other Heads and not 
necessarily under sala ry Head as otherwise they would not be able to create any new 
posts. 
8.   The Committee finally asked the Secretary, Ministry of Information and 
Broadcasting to furnish a note within ten days stating the extent to which they can agree 
to the view point of the Press Council of India and within what time the pending issues 
would be resolved. 
9.   In response to the oral evidence, the Ministry of Information and Broadcating vide 
their communication dated the 7 th February, 2002 furnished a detailed note giving the 
action taken by Government for resolving the outstanding issues as well as a comparative 
statement on the points under dispute in respect of the service regulation of the PCI 
Employees giving inter alia  the proposal of the Ministry, the counter proposa l of the 
Chairman, PCI and the proposal as approved by the Ministry of Finance (Annexure-II). 
In continuation of the status note, the Ministry of Information & Broadcasting on the 12th 
February, 2002 informed that the Ministry of Finance had agreed to the following 
formulation :- 
      ".... the Council may create other posts by effecting matching savings primarily 
from saving from salaries, but if the requirement of the post is extremely urgent, then 
from any head in the budget. 
      The powers to create such posts by the Council shall be subject to and be exercised 
in accordance with the General Financial Rules, 1963. Delegation of the Financial 
Powers Rules, 1978 and the extant orders/instructions of the Finance Ministry issued 
from time to time on the subject". 
10.On the 22nd October, 2002, the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting furnished a 
copy of the Gazette notification containing the Press Council of India (Terms of Service 
of Employees) Regulation, 2002. 
11.The Committee notes that the Ministry of Information & Broadcasting have finally 
been able to publish the Press Council of India (Terms of Service of Employees) 
Regulation, 2002. The Committee is, however, pained over the long delay that has taken 
place in this whole exercise despite its constant pursuance. The Committee would have 
appreciated if the initiative taken by the Ministry of Information & Broadcasting 
during the last 2-3 years had been taken earlier, in which case, the regulations would 
have come in place much earlier. 
 
ANNEXURE-I 
The Press Council Act, 1978----Implementation of 109th Report of the 
Committee on Subordinate Legislation, Rajya Sabha 
      The Press Council of India is a statutory autono mous body established by the Press 
Council of India Act, 1978 (37 of 1978) for the purpose of preserving the freedom of the 
Press and maintaining and improving the standards of newspapers and news agencies in 
India. The Council is not only independent of g overnment control, but exercises quasi -
judicial authority by virtue of the provisions of the above mentioned Act. Its functions 
are governed by the rules which the Govt. has to make in consultation with it once the 
Council is established. The Council is al so empowered to make regulations, not 

inconsistent with the Act and the Rules, regarding its functioning in respect of the matters 
enumerated in clauses (a) to (e) of Section 26 of the Act. As far as the employees of the 
Council are concerned, however, clause (b) and the proviso to Section 26 read with sub -
section (2) of Section 11 of the Press Council Act provide that the Council may make 
regulations not inconsistent with the Act and the Rules, specifying the terms and 
conditions of service of the employees appointed by the Council under sub -section (2) of 
Section 11 with the prior approval of the Central Government. The terms and conditions 
of such employees shall by determined by the said regulations. 
      In exercise of the powers conferred by clause (b ) and the proviso to Section 26 read 
with sub-secton (2) of Section 11 of the Press Council Act, The Press Council of India 
(Terms & Conditions of Service of the Employees) Regulations were drafted by the 
Council. The said draft Service Regulations were fo rwarded by the Secretariat of the 
Council, specifying the terms and conditions of service of its employees, way back in the 
year 1982 to the Government of India in the Ministry of Information & Broadcasting for 
its prior approval, before notifying the same  in the Official Gazette. The said approval 
has yet to be received by the Press Council on account of the fact that despite several Inter 
- Ministerial meetings held from time to time between the officers of the Ministry of 
Information & Broadcasting, the Ministry of Finance and the Council to discuss and sort 
out the matter, no consensus could be arrived at on some of the regulations. At this 
juncture, it would be pertinent to reproduce certain observations from the 57th Report 
of the Committee on Subordin ate Legislation, Rajya Sabha, presented to the House on 
22nd December, 1983 after examining the Press Council Act, 1978. 
21."The Committee finds it difficult to agree with the Government's plea that in the 
absence of regulations duly framed by the Press Co uncil, and approved by 
Government, there was no vacuum in so far as conditions of services of the Council's 
employees were concerned and that until the regulations are so made and notified 
the conditions of service governing the Central Government employee s were being 
applied to the Council's employees. The Committee feels that the Press Council has 
a specific and autonomous role to perform and conditions of service of its employees 
have to be drawn up independently in consonance with the nature of its functions...." 
      Subsequently, the Committee on Subordinate Legislation in its meeting held on 9th 
August 1995, expressed a deep sense of anguish over the situation that the government 
had taken nearly ten years in approving the regulations relating to the  terms and 
conditions of service of the employees of the Council despite the Committee having 
forwarded extracts of its Reports to the Ministry of Information & Broadcasting on 11th 
January, 1984. This was followed by the 109th Report of the Committee on S ubordinate 
Legislation presented to the House on 29.5.1995 wherein the Committee reiterated the 
observations made by it in the 57th Report, strongly recommending the notification of 
the draft service regulations at the earliest. 
      An Inter-Ministerial meeting was accordingly held on 1.8.1997 and the secretariat of 
the Council, as per the outcome of the said meeting, once again sent the draft regulation 
to the Ministry of Information & Broadcasting for its approval and thereafter notifying 
the same in the Official Gazette. A similar exercise was repeated by the Council after the 
Ministry again asked the Council to amend certain provision in the draft regulations, and 
on 24.1.2000 revised draft regulations were yet again sent to the Ministry. The approval 
of the Ministry concerned is, however, yet awaited. 
      It appears to the Press Council that the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting is 
desirous of curtailing the powers of the Council with regard to the creation of posts and 
amendment of the schedu le as incorporated in regulation 3(2). Regulation 3(2) reads as 
follows: 

"3(2)    The Council may make such amendments in the Schedule from the time to 
time as it thinks necessary, provided all proposals relating to emolument structure, 
including adoption of pay scales, allowances, and revision of pay scales, allowances 
and revision thereof, and creation of posts where the maximum stage of a pay scale 
exceeds Rs.15,200/- per month, shall be made with the prior approval of the Central 
Government". 
      It may be pointed out the Regulation 3(2) has its genesis in Rules 8 and 8A of the Press 
Council Rules, 1979 framed by the Central Government. Rule 8 stipulates that the 
employees of the Council shall enjoy the same terms and conditions of service and rights 
and privileges as the employees of the Central Government. By Notification dated 
2/8/1998, in exercise of the powers conferred on it by Section 25 of the Press Council Act, 
the Central Government, in consultation with the Press Council, inserted Rule 8A to the 
Press Council Rules, which reads as follows:- 
"8A(1) All proposals relating to emolument structure including adoption of pay 
scales, allowances, and revision of scales, allowances and revision thereof, and 
creation of posts where the maximum of pay scale exceeds Rs. 15,200/- p.m., shall be 
made only with the prior approval of the Central Government." 
      A bare reading of Rules 8 and 8A shows that, harmoniously construed, the effect of 
the said rules is that the Parliament in its wisdom gave autonomy to the Council in respect 
of the emolument structure, etc., of its employees, where the maximum of pay scale was 
below Rs. 4,500/- p.m. (i.e. Rs. 15,200/- p.m. under the Fifth Central pay Commission). In 
view thereof, regulations contrary to or inconsistent with the provisions of Rule 8A cannot 
be framed; nor can any executive instruction issued by the Ministry of Finance or by any 
other Ministry override the express provision of the Act and the Rules framed by the 
Legislature. Any attempt to do so will not  only have the effect of undermining the 
administrative autonomy granted to the Council by the Parliament having faith in its 
judiciousness, but will be contrary to the mandate of the legislature. 
      It is relevant to point out at this stage that the Co uncil has not resorted to 
indiscriminate augmentation of staff despite the onerous increase in its workload and its 
staff growth over the past 20 years has been quite meager. The Council has also more or 
less conceded to all the objections of the Ministry with regard to draft service regulations. 
The Council cannot, however, concede to a total abrogation of its powers, the Parliament 
having provided for the autonomy of the Council, nor it can consent to being treated as a 
subordinate/attached office of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting. This would 
reduce the Council to an appendage of the Government of India and altogether negate its 
functioning, which as stated above, is of a quasi -judicial nature and is meant to ensure 
the freedom of the press. 
 
ANNEXURE-II 
Developments in the matter of finalisation of service regulations 
of  PCI employees during the last one year 
      In view of delay in finalisation of service regulations of PCI employees, Chairman of 
the Raj ya Sabha Committee on Subordinate Legislation, had in June 2000, desired 
intervention of the then IBM for resolving the deadlock. The IBM met the Chairman, 
PCI, but on finding that agreement was not becoming possible, he replied in September, 
2000 that the Committee may direct the Press Council to notify regulations as approved 
by the Government. On 8th January, 2001, Secretary (I&B) and Secretary, PCI were 
called to appear before the Rajya Sabha Committee on Subordinate Legislation for 

explaining the reasons for delay in finalization of service regulations. The Committee was 
agreeable to issue the directions for notifying such regulations, as they find reasonable, 
provided both the Government and PCI undertake to abide by such directions. As the 
matter regarding creation of posts and Fixation of pay scales pertained to Ministry of 
Finance and Deptt. of Personnel & Training, no commitment was given by Secretary 
(I&B) to the Committee. The Committee desired this Ministry to indicate the extent of 
financial autonomy in regard to creation of posts and determination of pay scales, which 
could be granted to the Press Council. Besides, they also desired to know as to whether 
powers for creation of posts and determining pay scales can be made available to PCI to 
the extent it raises resources itself. 
      In pursuance thereof, on 10th January, 2001, Secretary (I&B) wrote to Secretary 
(Expenditure) and Secretary (DP&T) regarding giving a commitment to the Committee 
on Subordinate Legislation in the matter of direction s to be given by the Committee 
regarding power to create posts and fixation of pay scales. DP&T informed that the 
matter essentially concerned Ministry of Finance. On 1st February 2001, Ministry of 
Finance informed that the regulations to be issued in resp ect of PCI are required to be 
consistent with the Govt. policy with regard to statutory/autonomous bodies, as contained 
in Deptt. of Expenditure's O.M. of 15th October, 84 and 15th April, 94. These O.Ms. 
defined the limits of autonomy to be granted to autonomous bodies in matters concerning 
creation of posts and determining pay scales. M/o Finance advised that the Committee on 
Subordinate Legislation may keep these guidelines in view while giving any directions 
and it would not be desirable to deviate from general guidelines in respect of Press 
Council. On 23rd February, 2001, Secretary (I&B) discussed the issue with Chairman, 
PCI. During the meeting, Chairman, PCI was willing to place the concerns of the 
Government regarding the power to create posts before  the Council and was also 
agreeable to the suggestion that reference to the power to decide the emolument structure 
of PCI employees be deleted in the draft regulations. The Chairman suggested as a via 
media that while in principle the Government should agree to retain the power to create 
posts in the proposed regulations with the Council as provided in Rule 8A of Press 
Council Rules, a rider could be added that this power would be exercised with the prior 
approval of the Govt. whenever orders banning creation of posts are in force. Taking this 
as a reasonable suggestion, Secretary (I&B) forwarded modified regulations prepared 
accordingly (column 3 of the annexure) to Secretary (Expenditure) on 5th March 2001, 
for concurrence of Ministry of Finance. On 28th May, 2001, Ministry of Finance conveyed 
their concurrence to the proposed regulations. Immediately, thereafter, Chairman, PCI 
was requested by Secretary (I&B) to confirm discussions of 23rd February, 2001. On 12th 
June, 2001, the former Chairman, PCI infor med that there had been some 
misunderstanding about the discussions and that there was no question of the Council 
seeking prior approval from the Government for creation of posts at all levels, nor can 
there be any question of modification of the proposed regulation 3(2) as this would 
amount to total negation of the autonomy granted to the Council. He further mentioned 
that the maximum extent to which the Council may perhaps agree to vary the regulations 
is that it may consent to informing the Government about the creation of posts during the 
period the ban on creation of posts exists. 
      On 8th August, 2001, the present Chairman of Press Council, Shri Justice K. 
Jayachandra Reddy joined. Secretary (I&B) discussed the matter with the Chairman, 
PCI on 19th  September 2001. On 1st November, 2001, Chairman, PCI handed over a 
revised version of disputed service regulations (column 4 of the annexure) which was 
examined in the Ministry and slightly modified regulations (column 5 of the annexure) 
were sent to Chairman, PCI for confirmation. On 28th November, 2001, Chairman, PCI 
while agreeing to the formulation of regulations mentioned about changing the words 

'expenditure on salaries' to 'expenditure or salaries'. The draft regulations as suggested 
by Ministry and  corrected by Chairman, PCI did not find favour with Ministry of 
Finance. Secretary (I&B) discussed the matter with Secretary (Expenditure) and 
accordingly, on 25th January 2002, Ministry of Finance has agreed to the service 
regulations as indicated in column 7 of the annexure. 
          PCI has however not agreed to this as evident from the deliberations during the 
evidence of Secretary (I&B) and Secretary, PCI before the Rajya Sabha Committee on 
Subordinate Legislation on 28th January, 2002. The Committee has given ten days time 
to convey to them the final position of the Government on the matter. Secretary (I&B) 
had immediately moved Secretary (Expenditure) to consider that for creation of posts 
in PCI, matching savings may be offered primarily from savings from salaries, but, if 
the requirement of a post is extremely urgent, from any head in the budget and to delete 
the condition requiring that the posts against which matching savings are shown be 
vacant for less than one year. As desired, the crux of the sentiments expressed by the 
Hon'ble Members of the Committee were also brought to the notice of the Finance 
Ministry with the request that they be brought to the notice of the authority competent 
to take a decision in the matter. Response is awaited.

THE BORDER SECURITY FORCE (TENURE OF POSTING AND DEPUTATION) 
RULES, 2000-IMPLEMENTATION OF THE 138TH REPORT OF COMMITTEE 
      The Committee in its 138th Report, which was presented to the House on the 14th 
March, 2002, had examined the Border Security Force (Tenure of Posting and 
Deputation) Rules, 2000 and made the following observations :- 
"3.  The Committee is unhappy to note that the Ministry of Home Affairs did not 
frame statutory rules as contemplated under section 141 (2) of the Border Security 
Force Act, 1968 all this time upto the year 2000 and the executive instructions on 
posting/transfer of Border Se curity Force personal also appear to have been issued 
as late as in 1991-92 wherein it became difficult to manage the postings/transfers in 
the absence of statutory rules, The Ministry of Home Affairs should have gone in for 
statutory rules in the beginning itself. The Committee hopes that such situations will 
not reoccur. Further the Committee is not satisfied with the comments of Ministry 
of Home Affairs on Rule 2 (J) regarding definition of "family" and it recommends 
that dependent parents be made a part of 'family' after ascertaining the position with 
respect to other similarly situated organisations and the definition be amended 
suitably." 
2.   Relevant extracts from the 138th Report were frowarded to the Ministry of Home 
Affairs for compliance/necessary action on the 21st March, 2002. The Ministry on the 3rd 

April, 2002 sought extension of time till the 31 st August, 2002 to re -examine the matter. 
Thereafter, on the 10th October, 2002 they informed as under :- 
"As regards point no. III regarding inclusion of dependent parents in the definition 
of the family in rule - 2 (j) of the tenure rules, it is stated that the definition of family 
as given in the CCS Rules i.e. spouse, dependent children and dependent parents has 
been accepted and in order to  effect this amendment and certain problems in 
implementing different rules and provisions of the BSF (Tenure of Posting and 
Deputaion) Rules, 2000, a notification has been published in the Gazette of India on 
4.7.2002 amending the Principal Rules of 2000." 
3.                The Committee notes with satisfaction that the Ministry of Home Affairs 
vide their notification G.S.R. 264 dated 20th July, 2002 have since published 
the Border Security Force (Tenure of Posting and Deputation Amendment) 
Rules, 2002 (Annexure), Amending rule 2(j) of theBorder Security (Tenure of 
Posting and Deputation) Rules, 2000 by adding the dependent parents within 
the definition of the term "family".

THE JUTE MANUFACTURES DEVELOPMENT COUNCIL (PROCEDURAL) 
RULES, 1984----IMPLEMENTATION OF 136TH REPORT 
OF THE COMMITTEE 
      The Committee in its 136 th Report presented to the House on the 29 th August, 2001 
dealt with the Jute Manufactures Development Council (Procedural) Rules, 1984 and 
made the following recommendations : 
"The Committee notes with satisfaction that the Ministry of Textiles have agreed to 
carry out amendment in rules as follows on the basis of Committee's 
suggestions/recommendations : 
      (i)   Rule 4(1) by providing that the Chairman shall preside over the Meeting   of the 
Council. 
      (ii)  Rule 6(3) by providing that minutes containing a record of the business    would 
be circulated to the members for confirmation in the next meeting. 
      (iii)Rule 14(9) by providing for maintenance of a record of the business transacted by 
the Council. 
      (iv)Rule 11(1) by providing a period of three months for filling up a casual vacancy. 
      (v)  Rule 12 by deleting the provision with regard to appointment of the substitute 
member of the Council. 
      (vi)Rule 14(6) by providing that one third of the total number of members of the 
Council but not less that eleven members p resent shall form a quorum at a 
meeting of the Council. 
      (vii)      Rule 16(1) by revising salary limit from Rs. 1300 (pre-revised) to Rs. 13,500/- 
for purpose of creation and filling up of a post. 

      (viii)     Rule 16(2)(iii) by raising the limit of expenditure to be incurred outside India 
to the extent permissible under the Exchange Control Regulations or other 
relevant regulations and guidelines in place of the existing limit of   Rs. 10,000/-
. 
      (ix)Rule 19(2) by raising the ceiling on payme nts by the Council upto Rs. 5000/ - 
ordinarily and Rs. 20,000/ - extraordinarily in place of existing ceilings of Rs. 
1000/- and Rs. 2500/-, respectively. 
      (x)  Rule 19(6) by doing away with the provision requiring approval of Chairman/Vice 
Chairman for disposal of money placed in fixed deposit. 
       The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Textiles should carry out the 
above amendments expeditiously under intimation to it." 
2.   Extracts from the Report were forwarded to the Ministry of Textiles for 
implementation of the Committee's recommendations on the 5 th September, 2001. The 
Ministry of Textiles vide their O.M. dated the 4th June. 2002 informed that the rules as 
suggested by the Committee had been amended and notified vide notification G.S.R. 808 
(E) dated the 29th October, 2001 (laid on the Table of the Rajya Sabha on the 13th March, 
2002) containing the Jute Manufactures Development Council (Procedural) Rules, 2001. 
These rules were, however, found to be improper in its format. Hence, the Mi nistry of 
Textiles were asked to get them rectified vide this Secretariat O.M. dated the 2nd August, 
2002. After a couple of reminders, the Ministry vide their communication dated the 24th 
January, 2003 furnished a notification G.S.R.836 (E) dated the 24th  December, 2002 
publishing the Jute Manufactures Development Council (Procedural) Rules, 2002 
(Annexure). 
3.   The Committee is satisfied to note that the Ministry of Textiles have notified the 
following amendments as per its suggestions: 
(i)  in Rule 12(2) it has been incorporated that the Chairman will convene the meeting 
of the Council; 
(ii)in Rule 5(3)(iv) a provision has been made for circulation of minutes of the 
meeting; 
(iii)       in Rule 5(iv) it has been made mandatory to maintain minute books 
containing a record of the business transacted by the Council; 
(iv)       in Rule 10(1) it has been made mandatory that any casual vacancy in the 
membership of the Council by any reason shall be filled up by appointment by 
the Central Government within a period of three months from the date of arising 
of such vacancy; 
(v)Rule 12 regarding appointment of substitute member has been deleted; 
      (vi)in Rule 12(6) it has been provided that one -third of the total number of members 
of the Council but not less than eleven members present shall form a quorum at 
a meeting of the Council; 
      (vii)      in Rule 14(1) a provision has been made that no posts carrying the maximum 
salary beyond Rs. 13,500 per mensem shall be created or filled without the 
previous approval of the Central Government; 
      (viii)     in Rule 14(1)(iii) by giving powers to incur expenditure outside India upto an 
amount, as may be permissible under the exchange control regulations or other 
relevant regulations, and guidelines of the Central Government on each 
individual item; 

      (ix)in Rule 17(2) the ceiling on payments by or on behalf of the Council has been raised 
upto Rs.5000/- ordinarily and Rs.20,000/- in extra- ordinary conditions; and 
      (x)  in Rule 17(5) the provision requiring approval of Chairman/Vice Chairman for 
disposal of money placed in fixed deposits has been done away with. 
          The Committee, further, observes that there is a typographical error in the 
numbering of rule 14(2) which has been wrongly numbered as 14(1). The Committee 
desires the Ministry to issue a corrigendum to remove this error.

(i)  implement all decisions taken by the council;

esatablishments of the Council;

(viii)        administer the Provident Fund of the Council; 
(ix)undertake such other duties and exercise such othe r powers, as may, from 
time to time, be entrusted or delegated to him by the Council or the 
Chairman.

member of the Council shall hold office for a period of two years.

had not occurred.

address and on failure to inform the change to his address, the address given in the fi rst 
instance shall for all purposes be deemed to be his correct address.

Chairman to convene a meeting at any time:

time by the Chairman who shall inform in advance the Central Government and 
members of the subject matter for discussion and the reasons for which he considers it 
urgent. No other business shall be transacted at such special meeting. 
      (3) The Secretary shall, with the approval of the Chairman, or, in the absence of the 
Chairman, the Vice-Chairman, fix the date, time and place of every meeting of the 
Council and issue notice of the meeting giving at least ten clear days' notice. 
      (4) The Secretary shall, with the approval of the Chairman, or in the absence of 
Chairman, the Vice -Chairman, prepare and circulate amongst the members, at least 
seven days before a meeting of the Council, a list of the business to be transacted at such 
meeting. No business, not included in the agenda shall be considered at a meeting of the 
Council, without permission of the Chairman of the meeting. If any member desires to 
suggest any subject for discussion by the Council, he shall give at least ten clear days' 
notice. 
      (5) The Chairman, or in his absence, the Vice -Chairman, shall preside over the 
meetings of the Council: 
      Provided that where both the Chairman and Vice-Chairman are absent, the members 
present shall elect a member from among themselves to preside over the meeting. 
      (6) one-third of the total number of members of the Council bu t not less than eleven 
members present shall form a quorum at a meeting of the Council.

meeting, the opinion of the majority shall prevail. Each member of the Council shall have 
one vote. In case of any equality of votes, the Chairman, or the Vice-Chairman, or in the 
absence of both, the member presiding over such meeting shall have a second or a casting 
vote.
