II 
THE STATUTORY ORDER NO. 1076 (E) DATED THE 
DECEMBER 15, 1998 ISSUED UNDER THE JUTE PACKAGING 
MATERIALS (COMPULSORY USE IN PACKAGING COMMODITIES) 
ACT, 1987 — IMPLEMENTATION OF 127TH REPORTS 
OF THE COMMITTEE 
        The Committee examined the Statutory Order No. 1076 (E) dated the 15th December, 
1998 issued under the Jute Packaging Materials (Compulsory Use in Packing 
Commodities) Act, 1987 and included the subject matter in its 127 th Report which was 
presented to the Hou se on the 14 th March, 2000. The Committee in the said report 
observed as under: 
              “4.  The Committee considered the subject matter at its meeting held on 
February 23, 2000. The Committee notes with satisfaction that Government have 
been keeping in mind the interest of the jute farmers, workers and the end users by 
following the provisions of the Jute Packaging Materials (Compulsory Use in Packing 
Commodities) Act, 1987. The Committee, however, desires that the problems of the 
jute growers need to be looked into by Government more seriously so that they could 
get a fair return. In the opinion of the Committee, Government need to put in more 
efforts towards diversification and value addition in the Jute Sector so that the jute 
growers as well as the persons engaged in the trade in this sector are encouraged. 
              5.  As regards the constitution of the Standing Advisory Committee, the 
Committee is not in agreement with the position as stated by the Ministry of Textiles. 
The Committee feels that its suggestion to broad base the composition of the Standing 
Advisory Committee has the endorsement of the Apex Court of the country also and, 
therefore, there is all the more a ground to review the composition of the Standing 
Advisory Committee and amend the provisions of the Statutory Order. The Standing 
Advisory Committees might be inviting and hearing views of the concerned 
industries and user sectors while reviewing the mandatory Packaging Order, but in 
the opinion of the Committee representation of concerned industries and user sectors 
in the Standing Advisory Committee would lend better support to the cause.” 
2.     Relevant extracts from the 127 th Report were forwarded to the Ministry of Textiles 
for their comments/clarifications on the 21 st March, 2000. The Ministry on the 11 th 
August, 2000 informed as under: 
        “In accordance to the directions of the Hon’ble Supreme Court the Standing 
Committee is inviting comments and hearing the views of the concerned industries 
and user sectors after giv ing due notice through recognized office bearers of the 
associations, particularly when the question of review of the mandatory Packaging 
Order is considered. Their views are fully taken into account before taking any 
decision in this regard. The matter may therefore be treated as closed.” 
3.     The Committee at its meeting held on the 16 th May, 2002 considered the subject 
matter and expressed its dissatisfaction over the Ministry’s Action Taken Report in 
pursuance of its recommendation as contained in the  127th Report on the subject. The 
Committee noted that the Ministry had simply reiterated their earlier position and had 
not complied with the Committee’s recommendations to broad base the composition of 
the Standing Advisory Committee. The Committee decided that its recommendations on 
the subject be further reiterated. Accordingly, the Ministry was requested vide this 
Secretariat communication dated the 31st May, 2002 to review the position in the light of 
the Committee’s recommendations/observations and i ntimate the proposed course of 
action. 

4.     In response, the Ministry on the 21st October, 2002 requested for a copy of the Report 
as well as a copy of this Secretariat’s communication dated the 31st May, 2002 which were 
not traceable with them. These documents were duly furnished to the Ministry. 
5.     Thereafter, there was no response from the Ministry despite repeated reminders 
from this Secretariat until a D.O. letter was issued to the Secretary, Ministry of Textiles 
on the 7th July, 2003 requesting for the latest position with regard to the implementation 
of Committee’s pending recommendations. 
6.     The Ministry furnished the Action Taken Note on the 29 th July, 2003 stating as 
under: 
I.     Regarding interest of jute farmers, workers and users enga ged in the trade in the 
Jute Sector 
        “The Minimum Support Price (MSP) are fixed by the Government every year. The 
Minimum Support Price for TD-5 grade of jute growers in Assam had been raised from 
Rs. 810/- per quintal in 2001 -02 to Rs. 850/ - per quintal for the jute year 2002 -03. This 
has further been raised to Rs. 860/- per quintal for the jute year 2003-04. On the basis of 
MSP declared by Government, grade -wise price differentials are fixed by the Jute 
Commissioner for every jute year are being wi dely publicized through radio, television, 
newspapers and other media. 
        The Government of India has taken necessary steps towards diversification and 
value addition in the jute sector. In order to modernize the jute sector, Special Jute 
Development Programme (SJDF) with cent per cent Central Assistance has been 
launched. In addition, financial assistance is also provided under the Technology 
Upgradation Fund Schemes (TUFS). The Government also proposes to launch Jute 
Technology Mission (JTM) for the development of jute industry. For providing incentives 
to exporters, the Duty Entitlement Pass Book (DEPB) Scheme has also been extended to 
the jute sector.” 
II.    Regarding constitution of the Standing Advisory Committee 
        “The recommendation has been noted and will be considered while constituting the 
new Standing Advisory Committee.” 
7.     The reply of the Ministry was found not satisfactory and they were asked vide this 
Secretariat communication dated the 24 th September, 2003 to review the matte r with a 
view to suitably modifying the provisions of rule 3 of the Jute Packaging Materials 
(Compulsory use in Packaging Commodities) Rules, 1987 as well as the relevant 
provisions of the Statutory Order so as to prescribe therein the concerned industries and 
user Sectors to be represented in the Standing Advisory Committee. 
8.     The Ministry vide their communication dated the 18 th December, 2003  
have since informed as under:---- 
        “The Ministry of Textiles has no objection in modifying the provisions of Rule 3 of 
the Jute Packaging Materials Act, 1987 so that the concerned industries and user 
Sectors are to be represented in the Standing Advisory Committee (SAC) after the 
expiry of the tenure of the SAC which was constituted in May, 2001 and will remain 
valid for a period of three years till May, 2004.” 
9.     Committee’s observations/recommendations 
        The Committee expresses its displeasure over the non -serious attitude of the 
Ministry of Textiles in implementing the recommendations of the Committee as contained 
in its 127 th Report as a result of which the Committee had to repeatedly approach the 
Ministry for eliciting a proper response. The Committee is rather shocked that the 
Ministry, in their initial action taken note on the Committ ee’s report, had simply 

reiterated their earlier stand and when they were asked to review the position, they did 
not have even a copy of the Committee’s report. 
        The Committee expects that the Ministry of Textiles would act more responsibly 
while dealing with the recommendations of the Committee. The Committee, however, 
notes that the Ministry of Textiles have ultimately agreed to amend the provisions of Rule 
3 of the Jute Packaging Materials (Compulsory Use in Packaging Commodities) Rules, 
1987 in order to provide therein the industries and user sectors to be represented in the 
Standing Advisory Committee in pursuance of its recommendations.

THE OZONE DEPLETING SUBSTANCES (REGULATION AND CONTROL)

REPORT OF COMMITTEE ON SUBORDINATE  
LEGISLATION, RAJYA SABHA 
        The Ozone Depleting Substances (Regulation and Control) Rules, 2000 were 
examined and the Committee in its 138 th Report, which was presented to the House on 
the 14th March, 2002, recommended as follows:- 
        “The Committee notes with satisfaction that the Ministry of Environment and 
Forests have agreed to rectify the typographical error in Rule 2 (h) (i) defining the term 
“manufacture” and specifying a time limit in Rule 13 for completing th e process of 
registration, renewal and cancellation as suggested by the Committee. The Committee 
hopes that the Ministry would bring in these changes in the Rules at the earliest.” 
2.     The Ministry of Environment and Forests sought extension of time vide their 
communications dated the 10th September, 2002, 19th December, 2002 and 21st April, 2003 
seeking upto 22 nd December, 2003, 31 st March, 2003 and 30 th June, 2003 respectively, 
which was duly granted. 
3.     The Ministry of Environment and Forests vide their communication dated the 10 th 
September, 2003 forwarded Notification S.O. 996 (E) dated the 29 th August, 2003 
notifying the Ozone Depleting Substances (Regulation and Control) Amendment Rules,

149th Report which was forwarded to the Ministry of Finance (Insurance Division) on the

2.     The Ministry of Finance (Insurance Division) furnished the action taken note on the 
recommendations of the Committee on the 19th September, 2003 as follows:-----

under Regulation-2 should be incorporated in the Regulations. 
        Action Taken :  The Ministry have inserted regulatory Regulations providing as 
under 
        “The designated person shall grant or renew the licence within a period of three 
months from the date of application.” 
        Recommendation (ii) : That the reasons for the delay in grant/renewal of licence and 
the likely time for completing the process in regulation 3 (2) should be intimated to the 
applicant. 
        Action Taken  : The Ministry have inserted regulatory Regulations providing as 
under: 
        “The designated person shall, if the consideration of the application is likely to get 
delayed within 60 days of the receipt of application, inform the applicant the reasons 
for such a delay, and the likely time it would take to do so”. 
        Recommendation (iii) : That whenever an application is rejected, the reasons should 
be informed to the applicant.

(Licensing of Insurance Agents) Regulations, 2000 already cover this recommendation

Division, have notified amendments in the Insurance Regulatory and Development 
Authority (Licensing of Insurance Agents) Regulations, 2000 as recommended by it.

SUMMARY OF RECOMMENDATIONS 
I 
THE COCONUT DEVELOPMENT BOARD REGULATIONS, 1982—
IMPLEMENTATION OF THE 126TH REPORT OF THE COMMITTEE ON 
SUBORDINATE LEGISLATION, RAJYA SABHA 
        The Committee is unhappy to note that the notification of the Coconut Board Service 
Regulations has been delayed for so long despit e specific recommendations of the 
Committee, first in its 115th Report presented on the 24th November, 1997 and thereafter 
reiterated in its 126th Report presented to the House on the 23rd December, 1999. What is 
surprising is the fact that the Ministry of Finance had all along been objecting to allowing 
of the pension scheme on the Government of India pattern to the employees of the 
Coconut Development Board in utter disregard to the provisions of the Coconut 
Development Board Act as well as the regulation s framed thereunder. The Committee 
notes with regret that the Ministry of Agriculture approached the Ministry of Finance a 
number of times, but, every time the proposal was declined on the ground that they had 
taken a policy decision not to extend pension schemes to the employees of the autonomous 
institutions of all Ministries. The Committee is, however, satisfied that the Ministry of 
Finance reviewed their stand while tendering oral evidence before it on the 3 rd of 
September, 2003 and agreed to concur wit h the proposal of the Ministry of Agriculture 
to allow the benefit of pension on the lines of the Government of India to the existing 
employees of the Coconut Development Board till the notification of the service 
regulations keeping in view the legal posi tion and the administrative difficulties of the 
employees which would have otherwise entailed. The Committee would have appreciated 
if the Ministry of Finance had given this consideration to the matter earlier when the 
Ministry of Agriculture had been appr oaching them repeatedly for clearing of the 
regulations alongwith the legal opinion which was in their favour. 
II 
THE STATUTORY ORDER NO. 1076 (E) DATED DECEMBER 15, 1998 
ISSUED UNDER THE JUTE PACKAGING MATERIALS (COMPULSORY 
USE IN PACKAGING COMMODITIES) ACT, 1987—IMPLEMENTATION 
OF 127TH REPORT OF THE COMMITTEE 
        The Committee expresses its displeasure over the non -serious attitude of the 
Ministry of Textiles in implementing the recommendations of the Committee as contained 
in its 127 th Report as a re sult of which the Committee had to repeatedly approach the 
Ministry for eliciting a proper response. The Committee is rather shocked that the 
Ministry, in their initial action taken note on the Committee’s report, had simply 
reiterated their earlier stand and when they were asked to review the position, they did 
not have even a copy of the Committee’s report. 
        The Committee expects that the Ministry of Textiles would act more responsibly 
while dealing with the recommendations of the Committee. The Co mmittee, however, 
notes that the Ministry of Textiles have ultimately agreed to amend the provisions of Rule 
3 of the Jute Packaging Materials (Compulsory Use in Packaging Commodities) Rules, 
1987 in order to provide therein the industries and user sectors  to be represented in the 
Standing Advisory Committee in pursuance of its recommendations.

LAYING OF STATUTORY ORDERS ON THE TABLE OF RAJYA SABHA 
        During the 201 th Session of the Rajya Sabha, 42 Statutory Orders were laid on the 
Table of the House by various Ministries/Departments. The details of the Gazette 
Notifications in which these were publis hed and the date of their laying on the Table of 
the Rajya Sabha have been indicated in the Ministry-wise Statement (Annexure).

notifications laid, only one notifica tion at Sl. No. 13 laid by the Ministry of Human 
Resource Development, Department of Women and Child Development has been delayed 
by five months and no delay statement has been appended therewith. The Committee 
impresses upon the Ministry of Human Resource  Development (Department of Women 
and Child Development) to pay adequate attention towards the timely laying of the 
subordinate legislation and to append the delay statement in case there is a delay in laying.

Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (Department of 
Telecommunications) bear identical reference number. In this context, the Committee 
would like to invite the Ministry's attention to its fol lowing 
observations/recommendations as contained in the 152nd Report. 
"In the opinion of the Committee, every notification should be assigned a distinctive 
number in order to give it a separate identity and similarly, no notification should 
be published/la id which does not carry a notification number. The Committee 
expects all Ministries/Departments of Government of India to exercise caution in this 
regard. In case where there are more than one notifications under a single file, the 
Ministries/Departments s hould ensure that the file number on each notification 
should be suitably distinguished from one another". 
The Committee hopes that the Ministry of Information Technology (Department of 
Information Technology) would take suitable corrective measures for future.

2.     During the course of scrutiny of these Notifications/Orders, the Committee has noted 
some cases of abnormal delay ranging from 2 to 6 years between the date of notification 
of the Order and the date of its laying. The annexed statement also indicates the period 
of delay in cases where notifications have not been laid as per the schedule prescribed by 
the Committee and also whether such notifications were accompanied by any statement 
indicating the reasons for the delay in laying. The observations/recommendations of the 
Committee in respect of the specific Ministries/Departments are as follows:---- 
(i)     Ministry of Environment & Forests 
        The Committee notes with regret that the Ministry of Environment and Forests have 
delayed the laying of 6 of their notifications (Sl. No. 35 -37 and 41 -43) out of the 17 
notification laid by them during the 202 nd Session. The delay ranges between 10 months 
and 1 year 4 months. Further, the Ministry have appended the delay statement with 3 
notifications (Sl. No. 41 -43) only and the re maining 3 notifications (Sl. No. 35 -37) were 
not accompanied by delay statements. The Committee recommends that the Ministry of 
Environment & Forests should strictly adhere to the time schedule as recommended by 
it in its 131 st Report in laying of the Subo rdinate Legislation before Parliament and in 
case of any delay in laying of the notifications, a delay statement should also invariably 
be appended therewith. 
(ii)    Ministry of Finance 
        The Committee is unhappy to note that out of the 320 notifica tions laid by the 
Ministry of Finance during the 202 nd Session, there has been a delay in laying of 27 
notifications listed at Sl. Nos. 51-55, 131-138, 139, 140-143, 144, 145-146, 147, 148-151 and 
152 of the Annexure. The period of delay range from a minim um of 9 months to the 
maximum of 3 years and 6 months. The Committee views with serious concern that in 
spite of its repeated recommendations regarding the timely laying of subordinate 
legislation, there has not been any appreciable improvement in the position. 

        The Committee further notes that all the delayed notifications pertain to the 
Department of Economic Affairs (Banking Division). The reasons for delay which have 
been appended with some of these notifications, such as, “copies of the notifications were 
not received in time” are also not plausible enough to justify the delay that range between 
1-3 years. The Committee notes with regret that the Ministry of Finance have again failed 
to strictly adhere to the time schedule as prescribed in its 13 1st Report. The Committee 
hopes that the Ministry of Finance would put an effective mechanism in place to eliminate 
such instances of delay in future, particularly on account of delay in receiving printed 
copies of the notifications. The Committee hopes th at the Ministry of Finance would be 
able to plug the loopholes so that delays do not recur in future. 
(iii)   Ministry of Information and Broadcasting 
        The Committee notes that the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting laid two 
notifications (Sl.  Nos. 392 and 393) and both were delayed by more than one year. 
Further, the Ministry did not append any delay statement with these notifications. The 
Committee recommends that the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting should take 
note of the time schedule as prescribed by it for laying of the Subordinate legislation and 
take necessary corrective steps so that such instances do not recur. 
(iv)   Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions 
        The Committee notes with regret that the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances 
and Pensions delayed the laying of 11 notifications (Sl. Nos. 409 -419) out of 16 laid by 
them during the 202nd Session. Further, none of the delayed notification was accompanied 
by a delay statement. The period of delay wa s also substantial, ranging between 1 to 2 
years. The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances 
and Pensions should take necessary corrective steps in the right earnest so that they are 
able to lay their Subordinate Legislation  on time. The Committee further recommends 
that the Ministry should invariably apprise the House about the reasons for delay 
through delay statement in case they are unable to lay any ‘Order’ on time. 
3.     The Committee also notes that there has been delay in laying of one notification each 
by the Ministries of Health and Family Welfare (Sl. No. 371), Home Affairs (Sl. No. 376), 
Human Resource Development (Sl. No. 386), Labour and Employment (Sl. No. 394), 
Railways (Sl. No. 444), Shipping, Road Transport and Highways (Sl. No. 538) and Urban 
Development (Sl. No. 593). In case of notification at Sl. No. 538 (Ministry of Shipping, 
Road Transport and Highways) the delay is of 6 years and 11 months. Further, the 
notifications at Sl. Nos. 386, 394 and 593 were not accompanied by delay statements. The 
Committee hopes that these Ministries would devise appropriate measures to cut on the 
delay in    laying of the notifications. They should also be particular to append delay 
statement in case the laying of Subordinate Legislation is delayed. 
4.     Besides, the timely laying of Subordinate Legislation, the Committee has been 
consistently reiterating that each notification should have a distinctive number so that 
the same is identifiable. However, during the 202nd Sessi on the Committee has came 
across three instances where the notifications were laid without a distinct number. These 
notifications pertain to the Ministry of Communications & Information Technology (Sl. 
No. 19), the Ministry of Finance (Sl. No. 132) and the  Ministry Human Resource 
Development (Sl. No. 390). The Committee reiterates that every notification should have 
a distinctive number to give it a separate identity. The Committee  recommends that such 
instances should not be repeated and Ministries/ Depar tments should ensure that every 
notification is assigned a distinct number so that the same is identifiable at any later stage. 
5. The Committee impresses upon all the Ministries/Departments to take immediate steps 
to ensure timely and proper laying of sub ordinate legislation. The Committee, 

accordingly, wishes to bring to the notice of all Ministries/Departments of the 
Government of India, particularly, the defaulting ones, the following recommendations, 
as contained in its 131st, 135th and 152nd Reports: 
“Orders required to be laid before the House should be laid  
(i) if the House is not in Session, during the Session immediately following the date 
of publication of the Order in the Official Gazette and (ii) if the House is in Session, 
on the date of the p ublication of the Order, during its continuance and in case the 
time lag between the date of publication and the date of the closing of the Session is 
less than 15 clear days, before the expiry of the Session immediately following the 
said Session. All the  Ministries/Departments of Government of India should 
henceforth comply with this schedule in the matter of laying of the Orders issued 
under various Acts of Parliament on the Table of the Rajya Sabha.”    
                                                                                    (131st Report) 
“The Committee has, time and again, emphasized that it is essential that in case there 
is a delay in the laying of Statutory Orders, the concerned Ministry/Department 
should invariably append a delay statement along with the notifications being laid so 
as to apprise Parliament of the causes of delay. The Committee desires all 
Ministries/Departments to take a note of this, since the intension is that through the 
process of formulation of a delay statement the Ministry is able to introspect, 
identifying bottlenecks and devise remedial 
measures”.                                                                                   (135th Report) 
“In the opinion of the Committee, every notification should be assigned a distinctive 
number in order to give it a separate identity and similarly, no notification should be 
published/laid which does not carry a notification number. The Committee expects 
all Ministries/ Departments of Government of India to exercise caution in this regard. 
In case where there are more than one notification under a single file, the Ministries/ 
Departments should ensure that the file number on each notification should be 
suitably distinguished from one another. 
                                                                                  (152nd Report)

have been persued by the Committee in the light of the provisions of 
the Acts under which these were framed and also with a view to seeing

I

2. During the course of scrutiny of these Orders, the Committee has 
noted some cases where there has been a considerable time lag between 
the date of notification of the Order and the date of its laying. The 
annexed statement also indicates the period of delay in cases where 
notifications have not been laid as per the Comm ittee’s guidelines and 
whether such notifications were accompanied by a statement indicating 
the reasons for the delay in laying. In some of the cases the delay has 
been quite abnormal. The observations/recommendations of the 
Committee in respect of the sp ecific Ministries/Departments are as 
follows: 
(i) Ministry of Agriculture 
 (Department of Agriculture and Cooperation) 
 The Committee is unhappy to note that out of the 4 notifications 
laid by the Ministry of Agriculture (Department of Agriculture and 
Cooperation) there has been a delay of upto 1 year in the laying of three 
notifications (Sl. Nos. 2, 3, 4 of the Annexure). The Ministry have not 
appended delay statement with any of these delayed notifications.  The 
Committee recommends that the Ministry of Agriculture (Department 
of Agriculture and Cooperation) should stick to the time schedule as 
recommended by it in its 131 st Report in the matter of laying of 
Subordinate Legislation before Parliament and in case of any delay, the 
delay statement must also be appended therewith. 
(ii) Ministry of Commerce and Industry (Department of 
Industrial 
 Policy and Promotion) 
 The Committee regrets to note that the Ministry of Commerce and 
Industry (Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion) have 
delayed the laying of 7 of their notifications (Sl. Nos. 
17,18,20,21,22,23,and 24) out of the 14 notifications laid by them during 
the session. The Ministry have not appended delay statement with six 
of the delayed notifications where the delay ranges from 6 months to 1 
year and three months. The Ministry have appended delay statement 
only with 1 notification (Sl. No.21) stating therein as follows: 
“The copy of the above notification could not be laid in the earlier 
session as the printed copies of the notification were not received 
in time. Subsequent session i.e. Budget Session of Parliament, 2004 
took place for one week only for vote on accounts. Next Parliament 

Session was convened during July-August, 2004 after constitution 
of the new Lok Sabha. At that time we missed th e laying down of 
the notification due to oversight. The delay is regretted”. 
 The Committee is not convinced with the grounds for delay 
furnished by the Ministry of Commerce & Industry in the delay 
statement. The Committee hopes that the Ministry would take 
necessary corrective measures to avoid delay in laying on such grounds 
and adhere to the schedule prescribed by the Committee in its 131st 
Report. 
(iii) Ministry of Communications and Information 
Technology 
 The Committee is unhappy to note that  out of the 20 notifications 
laid by the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology, 
there has been a delay in the laying of 15. The Department of 
Telecommunications have delayed the laying of 2 notifications (Sl. Nos. 
26, 27) out of the 4 notifications laid by them and have appended delay 
statement with both. The delay statement appended to notification 
No.414/7/99-FA dated 23rd February, 2004 (Sl. No.26) states: “....After 
notification of the Regulation in the Official Gazette, TRAI sent the 
Regulation to the Department of Telecommunications on 4th October, 
2004. Accordingly, the reason for delay in laying the Regulation on the 
Table of the House is due to delayed submission to the Government”. 
The delay in laying of notification No. 414 - 7/99 - FA dated 25th May, 
2004 (SI. No. 27) has been attributed by the Ministry to the delay in 
making available the copies of the notifications to the Government. The 
Committee hopes that the Government would take necessary corrective 
measures to avoid such in stances of delay which are, even otherwise, 
not very convincing. 
 On the other hand, the Department of Information Technology 
have delayed the laying of 13 notifications (Sl. Nos. 29 to 41) out of the 
16 notification laid by them. The Committee regrets to note that the 
delay in the laying of the notifications by the Department of 
Information and Technology range from 9 months to around a year in 
some cases and upto 1 year and 9 months in others. The Ministry have 
even failed to append the delay statement to the notifications despite so 
much delay. The Committee recommends that the Ministry of 
Communications & Information Technology should avoid such delays 
in future and append delay statement where ever the schedule as laid 

down by the Committee on Subordinate Legislation, Rajya Sabha in its 
131’t Report is not adhered to. 
(iv) Ministry of Company Affairs 
 The Committee regrets to note that there is a delay of 11 months 
in laying of one out of the five notifications laid by the Ministry of 
Company Affairs (Sl No. 47). The Committee hopes that the Ministry 
of Company Affairs would avoid such instances in future. 
(v) Ministry of Environment and Forests 
 The Committee notes with regret that the Ministry of Environment 
and Forests have laid 8 notifications during the ‘session and out of them 
4 (SI. Nos. 57, 60, 61, 62) have been delayed by a period of 4 to 7 months. 
Further, the Ministry have appended delay statement with only 2 of the 
delayed notifications (Sl. Nos. 61,62). The Committee observes that the 
delay in  laying of the Rules was “owing to the pre -mature sine die  
adjournment of the House.” The Committee hopes that the Ministry of 
Environment and Forests would take action at the first available 
opportunity so as to obviate such eventualities. 
(vi) Ministry of Finance 
 The Committee notes that out of the 211 notifications laid by the 
Ministry of Finance during the Winter Session, 2004, there has been a 
delay in the laying of 11 notifications (Sl Nos. 65, 66, 98 to 102, 124, 170 
to 172). The Committee further notes that the Ministry have appended 
delay statement in only two cases. While the delay in the laying of 
notification No. LEG -59/46 dated the 22nd July, 2004 (Sl. No.66) has 
been attributed to sine die  adjournment of the House, the delay 
statement appended to notification No 8/5/2004 - IF - I dated the 18th 
June, 2004 (Sl. No. 124) states as follows: 
 “Two notifications were sent to the Controller of Publications, 
Civil Lines, New Delhi vide letter dated 26th May, 2004 for 
publishing in the Gazette of India. One notification under sub -
section (1) of Section 18 of the Industrial Development Bank of 
India Act, 1964 and another notification under sub -section (2) of 
Section 21 of the said Act. 
 Ministry of Urban Development, Dep artment of Publications 
Civil Lines has forwarded one notification vide letter dated 12th 
July, 2004. It was found that only one notification under Section 18 

of the IDBI Act, 1964 had been published and the other notification 
under Section 21 of the said Act had not yet been published. A 
reminder was sent to the Controller of Publication, Civil Lines vide 
letter dated 26th July, 2004. Therefore, these notifications could not 
be laid on the Table  of both Houses of Parliament during 
Budget Session of Parliament. 
 After authentication by Minister of State (R), the notification 
will be laid on the Table of both Houses of Parliament during the 
Winter Session of Parliament.” 
 The Committee hopes that the Ministry of Finance would avoid 
such instances of delay in  the laying of Subordinate Legislation and 
shall keep the House informed of the reasons for delay in laying 
through delay statements in all cases. 
(vii) Ministry of Health and Family Welfare 
 The Committee regrets to note that the Ministry of Health and 
Family Welfare have delayed the laying of one notification (Sl. No. 276) 
by 9 months out of the 2 notifications laid during the Session. The 
Ministry have appended a delay statement. The Committee would like 
to draw the attention of the Ministry of Health an d Family Welfare to 
the Schedule prescribed by the Committee in the matter of laying of 
Subordinate Legislation in its 131st Report (relevant extracts 
reproduced in para 3 of the report) and hopes that the same shall be 
complied with. 
(viii) Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions 
 The Committee notes with regret that the Ministry of Personnel, 
Public Grievances & Pensions have laid 26 notifications during the 
Session out of which 12 (Sl. Nos. 289 to 300) have been delayed by 
almost 1 year. The Ministry have appended delay statement with all the 
12 delayed notifications. In their delay statement appended to the 
notification at Sl. No. 300 of the Annexure the Ministry have submitted 
as follows: 
 “The Notification which was sent to the Government o f India 
Press for Publication in Part II section 3(i) of the Gazette of India 
on 5th November, 2003 was published in the Gazette on 13th 
December, 2003, i.e. during the Winter Session of Parliament, 
2003. Therefore it was not possible to lay the notificati on during 
the Winter Session of Parliament, 2003. 

 The notification was sent for laying on the Table of the Lok 
Sabha/Rajya Sabha during the Budget Session of Parliament 2004, 
which commenced from the 5th July, 2004 and scheduled to end on 
September, 2004. However, due to pre -mature sine-die 
adjournment of Parliament on 26 th August, 2004, the notification 
could not be laid on the Table of the House”. 
 The Committee is unhappy to note that the Ministry of Personnel, 
Public Grievances & Pensions could not avail of the opportunity to lay 
the Subordinate Legislation not only during the Winter Session 2003 
but also during the Budget Session 2004 which actually had 22 sittings. 
In any case, had the Ministry acted promptly they could have 
accomplished their job in the earlier part of the Budget Session 2004. 
The Committee hopes that the Ministry of Personnel, Public 
Grievances & Pensions would be meticulous in future in complying 
with time schedule as prescribed by the Committee and take prompt 
action, rather than keeping the work pending towards the end of the 
Session. 
(ix) Ministry of Railways 
 The Committee notes with regret that out of the 13 notifications 
laid by the Ministry of Railways, there has been a delay in the laying of 
11 notifications (Sl. Nos.324 to 334). The Committee expects the 
Ministry of Railways to exercise caution in the matter of timely laying 
of subordinate Legislation and ensure that the schedule as prescribed 
by it in this behalf is followed  meticulously and in case of any delay in 
the laying thereof, a delay statement must be appended there with 
without fail. 
(x) Ministry of Shipping, Road Transport and Highways 
 The Committee regrets to note that out of a total of 92 notifications 
laid by M inistry of Shipping, Road Transport and Highways, during 
the 203rd Session there has been a delay in the laying of 13 notifications 
(SI. Nos.336, 343 to 352, 424 and 426). The delay in laying of the 
notifications ranges between 5 months to 1 year. The Comm ittee 
observes that while notification No. D1201 1/1/98 - TAMP at Sl. No. 426 
of the annexure could not be laid during the Budget Session due to sine 
die adjournment of Parliament, the delay statement appended to the 
rest of the delayed notifications does not carry convincing reasons. The 
delay statement appended to one set of notifications (S.O. 751 (E), 

S.0.862 (E) to S.0.868 (E), S.0.885 (E); S.O. 579 (E), S.0.811 (E), S.0.912 
(E), S.0.934 (E), S.0.935 (E) and S.0.938 (E)) states, “It took some time 
to collect the papers and complete the procedural formalities”. For 
example the delay statement appended to G. 5.R.83 (E) dated the 28 th 
January, 2004 states, “Since the requisite number of copies of the 
printed notifications were not received in time, the sa me could not be 
laid on the Table of the House.” The Committee directs the Ministry of 
Shipping, Road Transport and Highways to be more prompt and 
vigilant in the laying of rules/regulations within the stipulated period 
and evolve some systematic procedure to avoid such instances in future. 
3. The Committee impresses upon all the Ministries/Departments to 
take immediate steps to ensure timely and proper laying of subordinate 
legislation. The Committee, accordingly, wishes to bring to the notice 
of all Ministries/Departments of the Government of India, particularly, 
the defaulting ones, the following recommendations, as contained in its 
131st 135th and 152nd Reports: 
 “Orders required to be laid before the House should be laid (i) if 
the House is not in Sessi on, during the Session immediately following 
the date of publication of the Order in the Official Gazette and (ii) if 
the House is in Session, on the date of the publication of the Order, 
during its continuance and in case the time lag between the date of 
publication and the date of the closing of the Session is less than 15 clear 
days, before the expiry of the Session immediately following the said 
Session. All the Ministries/Departments of Government of India should 
henceforth comply with this schedule in  the matter of laying of the 
Orders issued under various Acts of Parliament on the Table of the 
Rajya Sabha.” 
(131st Report) 
 “The Committee has, time and again, emphasized that it is 
essential that in case there is a delay in the laying of Statutory Order s, 
the concerned Ministry/Department should invariably append a delay 
statement along with the notifications being laid so as to apprise 
Parliament of the causes of delay. The Committee desires all 
Ministries/Departments to take a note of this, since the intension is that 
through the process of formulation of a delay statement the Ministry is 
able to introspect, identifying bottlenecks and devise remedial 
measures”. 
(135th Report) 

“In the opinion of the Committee, every notification should be assigned 
a distinctive number in order to give it a separate identity and similarly, 
no notification should be published/laid which does not carry a 
notification number. The Committee expects all 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India to exercise caution in 
this regard. In case where there are more than one notification under a 
single file, the Ministries/Departments should ensure that the file 
number on each notification should be suitably distinguished from one 
another. 
(152nd Report)

TENTH MEETING 
The Committee met at 11.30 A.M. on Tuesday the 12 th April 2005 in Room No. 126 -
C (Chairman’s Room), Third Floor, Parliament House, New Delhi. 
MEMBERS PRESENT 
 1. Shri A. Vijayaraghavan 
 2. Shri Nabam Rebia 
 3. Shrimati Sukhbuns Kaur

 9.  Shri Harendra Singh Malik

  SECRETARIAT 
 1. Shri Deepak Goyal, Deputy Secretary 
 2. Shri Ram Behari Gupta, Under Secretary 
 3. Ms. S. Pankajavalli, Committee Officer. 
1. The Committee took up for consideration its draft 156 th Report on Statutory 
Orders laid on the Table of Rajya Sabha during its 203rd session. While considering 
the draft report, the Committee noted persistent default on the part of certain 
Ministries/Departments in the laying of their subordinate legislation despite 
Committees’ recommendations/observations from time to time. The Committee, 
accordingly, desired that the lay ing of Subordinate Legislation by the 
Ministries/Departments over the past 5 to 6 sessions may be reviewed and the 
representatives of major defaulting Ministries/Departments could be invited before 
the Committee for clarifications. With this note, the Comm ittee adopted its Draft 
156th Report. 
2. Next, the Committee took up for consideration its draft 157 th Report on certain 
Rules and Regulations examined by it. The Committee adopted the draft report after 
some discussion. 
3. The Committee decided to present  both the reports to the House on 20 th April 
2005 and authorised its Chairman and in his absence Shri R. Shunmugasundaram 
and Shri Ravula Chandra Sekar Reddy, MPs, to present the report to the House. 
4. The Committee thereafter considered its future programme and decided to hear 
in its next meeting the representatives of the Small Scale Pharmaceuticals 
Manufacturers Association on the Drugs and Cosmetics (8th Amendment) Rules 2001. 
5. The Committee also decided to undertake a study visit to Hyderabad, Bangalore 
and Coimbatore in the last week of May 2005 in connection with the rules and 
regulations presently under its examination. 
6. The Committee then adjourned at 12.15 P.M.

INTRODUCTION

. 
1.2  The Committee considered and adopted the Report in its meeti ng held on 12 th

1.3  The matters   examined by the Committee arise out of the scrutiny of various
